## X.3 `_recheck()` inside the write transaction

`Airline.book` → conversation lock → `Store.write()` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) → `_book()` →
`_recheck()`. B6 re-validates the quote on the current `locations.db`: strict content hash, and a
graph rebuild when the hash changed, then the itinerary price and a fresh cheapest-route search —
all **while app.db's write lock is held**. Since 06 P2-7 a changed file is normally loaded just
before the transaction, so inside it only the hash and the route search run (sub-millisecond on
711 cities). If the file changes between that pre-load and the re-check, the full rebuild
(~130 ms measured) happens inside the transaction and every other writer — messages, call logs,
other bookings — waits for it. The benchmark forces exactly that case (`changed inside
transaction`) to measure it.

**Candidate optimisation, not implemented (needs its own review against B1–B7):** run the
re-check before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and keep only a cheap, consistent check inside:
1. Before the transaction: `net = networks.current(strict=True)`; compute `(fingerprint,
   problem) = recheck(quote, net)`. The quote's legs, price and origin/destination are immutable
   once stored, so this depends only on the quote and `net`.
2. Inside the transaction: all state checks stay where they are (B1–B5: owner, status, expiry,
   nonce — they read rows another writer may change). Then re-hash `locations.db` (strict, no
   rebuild): if the hash still equals `fingerprint`, the pre-computed result is the result of a
   re-check made now; if it differs, either redo the full re-check inside (today's behaviour, rare)
   or refuse with a retryable `data_unavailable` and let the click be repeated.
3. **TOCTOU:** the window "file changes after the in-transaction hash, before COMMIT" exists
   today as well (B6 means "fresh at booking time", the time of the hash); the window "file changes
   after the pre-computation, before the transaction" is closed by step 2's hash comparison. The
   quote row cannot change in between except its status, which is still checked inside. So B6
   keeps its meaning, while the write lock is no longer held across a rebuild or route search.
   Cost: one extra hash of a 60 KB file per click.

## X.4 Why this is a conscious trade-off

SQLite + one worker gives atomic booking with one transaction and two constraints, no database
server to run, back up or secure, and an operational footprint of one file — the right size for a
take-home and a single-VPS demo. It is **not** a measured production scalability guarantee: the
benchmark below shows where it holds on one machine, not what a real airline workload needs.

## X.5 Benchmark (`backend/bench/`)

Reproducible, isolated, no LLM cost: `cd backend && nice -n 10 uv run python -m bench`
(`--quick` for a smoke run; `tests/test_bench.py` runs a tiny one in CI).
- **Setup:** per level a fresh app.db and a private copy of `locations.db` in a temp dir; fixed
  seed; 100 users with a conversation, history and presented quotes with nonces; the real app in
  its own uvicorn process (one worker, production limits) with a deterministic fake LLM (one
  `quote_route` call + a reply per turn, so each turn writes what a real one does).
- **Instrumentation:** `app.store.db.set_timing_hook` (off by default; one global lookup per
  operation when off) reports per transaction the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` wait, hold time to COMMIT,
  total time and outcome (commit / rollback / busy / timeout), tagged with the calling function.
  `_recheck`, `NetworkProvider.current` and graph rebuilds are timed by wrappers installed in the
  bench server process only (no airline code changes).
- **Scenarios:** mixed 70 % reads (history, tickets, conversation list) / 20 % chat turns / 10 %
  bookings, closed loop, 1/5/10/25/50/100 clients, warm-up + 3 measured intervals; booking burst
  (all clients click distinct quotes at once); same conversation (4 identical clicks per quote at
  once, 3 concurrent turns per conversation, a turn and a click at once); `locations.db` unchanged
  / changed before the click / changed inside the booking transaction; the mixed load with a
  simulated model latency per LLM step; an in-process writer microbenchmark.
- **Metrics:** throughput, p50/p95/p99 per endpoint, write-lock wait and hold p50/p95/p99 (also
  per call site), `_recheck` and rebuild p50/p95/p99, BUSY / timeout / 5xx counts, server CPU and
  RSS, WAL size, and integrity checks that must be 0: double bookings, booked without ticket,
  ticket without booked quote or used nonce, client 200 without ticket (and vice versa),
  interleaved turns.

**Measured** (one run, 2026-11-24, Apple M4 10-core, macOS, Python 3.12, SQLite 3.47, APFS; full
tables in [results/bench-2026-11-24.md](results/bench-2026-11-24.md); the machine also ran other
agents, so treat single numbers as ±30 %):
- **Correctness held everywhere:** 0 double bookings, 0 quote/ticket mismatches, 0 client 200s
  without a ticket, 0 interleaved turns, 0 BUSY, 0 5xx — over the whole sweep, bursts of up to 300
  simultaneous clicks, 4 identical clicks per quote (exactly one success each; the rest
  `already_booked` / `conversation_busy`) and 3 concurrent turns per conversation.
- **Write transactions are short:** hold p50 ≈ 0.5–1.6 ms, p99 ≤ 34 ms at every level;
  ~250–290 write transactions/s at 25–100 clients. The in-process microbenchmark reaches
  ~3,000 commits/s with one insert per transaction.
- **The tail is lock *waiting*, not lock holding.** Write-lock wait p99 grows to 260–580 ms at
  10–25 closed-loop clients (and 600 ms with 64 threads in the microbenchmark, where hold p99 is
  0.4 ms). SQLite's busy handler polls with growing sleeps instead of queueing waiters, so an
  unlucky writer sleeps while others take the lock. Cheap remedy if it ever matters: an
  in-process FIFO lock in front of `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (valid only with one worker).
- **The process, not SQLite, saturates first.** Throughput peaks at ~200 req/s at 50 clients with
  the single worker at 150–340 % CPU (Python, JSON rendering of growing histories, the 32-thread
  executor); at 100 clients it drops to ~160 req/s while write hold stays ~0.5 ms. With 1 client,
  one conversation grows by ~100 turns during the run, so history/chat latency there measures
  history size more than concurrency.
- **`_recheck` is cheap unless the network is rebuilt:** p50 0.2 ms with `locations.db`
  unchanged. A rebuild takes ~140 ms; when it happens inside the booking transaction (forced in
  30 of 32 bookings in the `changed inside transaction` mode, and 3 of 26 rebuilds even in
  `changed before click` because of concurrent changes) it holds the write lock ~140–195 ms, and
  other writers' lock wait p99 rises from 0.47 s to 2.8 s. That is the case X.3 removes.
- **With model latency (0.6 s per LLM step, simulated):** at 10 clients the app is model-bound
  (chat p50 1.3 s, write-lock wait p99 47 ms); at 50 / 100 clients 16 % / 49 % of turns get
  `server_busy` from the 8 turn slots long before app.db matters (write wait p99 40 / 196 ms).
- Timing hook overhead when on: within noise (~423 vs 429 µs per read transaction; a read
  transaction costs ~0.4 ms, mostly opening the connection).

## X.6 When to change what

All thresholds below are **illustrative service SLOs** for deciding, not measured results and not
requirements of the take-home. Measure on the target host with `python -m bench` against them.

| Decision | Do it when (example SLO, sustained at the expected peak) | What it costs / what to keep |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep SQLite as is** | integrity checks 0; write-lock wait p99 < 100 ms; booking p99 < 500 ms; 0 BUSY and 0 5xx; one worker's CPU is not the limit | nothing |
| **Shorten write transactions first** (X.3 re-check outside the lock; batch or move LLM / tool call logs out of the request path) | write-lock wait p99 above the SLO while CPU has headroom, or the measured `changed inside transaction` case breaks the booking SLO | review against B1–B7 and the TOCTOU argument in X.3; model test + regression test |
| **More than one worker / machine** | one process's CPU is saturated (the sweep's CPU column), or availability needs two instances | the per-conversation lock must move into the database (advisory lock or conversation version) first; SQLite on shared storage is not an option across machines |
| **Move app.db to PostgreSQL** | multi-instance is required, or sustained writes exceed what one SQLite writer serves within the SLO after the step above, or operations need managed backups / PITR / replicas | row locks help different quotes and conversations, but locking, idempotency (`ON CONFLICT`), transactions and schema migrations must be redone and re-verified (B1–B7); a server to run. A graph database or MCP does not address app.db write contention |

**Applied to the measured run (example SLO of the first row):** met at 1 and 5 closed-loop clients
(≈ 85 req/s, ≈ 18 chat turns/s, booking p99 93 ms, wait p99 63 ms); missed from 10 clients on by
the lock-wait tail and from 50 on by process CPU. With realistic model latency the turn slots
limit the load first (≈ 5–6 completed turns/s), and write-lock wait p99 stays ≤ 50 ms up to 50 clients.
**Decision for the demo: keep SQLite and one worker.** Next steps only if a measured target
workload needs them, in this order: (1) re-check outside the write lock (X.3) and/or a FIFO
writer lock; (2) more workers only after the conversation lock moves into the database; (3)
PostgreSQL when multi-instance or operations require it. No QPS threshold here is a fact about
production.
# State invariants

Booking and confirmation rules are checked by model-based tests: a small reference model plus seeded random event
sequences, every invariant asserted after every event. A new state bug gets a new rule id here first, then a test.
Design context: `docs/design/design.md` §6.

## Event alphabet
`quote(user, conv, origin, dest)`, `stream_done(conv)` (cards presented, nonces issued),
`user_message(conv, text)` (incl. negations and questions), `llm_request_booking(conv, quote)`,
`click_book(user, quote, nonce)`, `click_book_concurrent(user, quote, nonce)`, `replay_nonce(quote, nonce)`,
`clock(+Δ)`, `db_change(kind)` (leg removed / coordinate moved / unrelated row changed / file replaced),
`other_user_click(quote, nonce)`, `disconnect_reconnect(conv)`, `stop_turn(conv)` (R6).

## B. Booking
- **B1 Ownership.** A ticket exists only if its quote belongs to the user who clicked.
- **B2 Presented.** A ticket exists only if its quote reached `presented` (its full card was sent with `done`) before the click.
- **B3 Click only.** Every ticket is caused by exactly one `click_book` with a valid, unused nonce for that quote; no
  other event (in particular `llm_request_booking`, any `user_message`) ever creates a ticket.
- **B4 Validity.** No ticket for a quote older than 15 minutes at click time.
- **B5 Idempotent.** At most one ticket per quote, under replay and concurrent clicks.
- **B6 Fresh.** A ticket's legs, coordinates, distance and price strings equal a fresh recomputation on the
  `locations.db` current at click time, and the route is still the cheapest; otherwise the quote is `stale` and no ticket.
- **B7 Atomic.** Quote status and tickets never disagree: `booked` ⇔ exactly one ticket.

## Q. Quotes
- **Q1 No supersede.** Creating a quote never changes the status of another quote.
- **Q2 Button state.** The button state a client sees (after `done` or reconnect) equals the server's quote state;
  a card of a `cancelled` message is never bookable (R6).
- **Q3 Terminal.** `booked`, `expired`, `stale` never change again.

## Process
- Seeds are fixed in CI. A failing seed prints its shrunk sequence and is kept as a named regression case.
- Layers: pure model test over `airline/` → API driven with fakes (clock, LLM, locations.db copy) → UI scenario
  (ego-browser) for the click path.

## U. Usage limits
- **U1 Daily cap.** For every user and UTC day, messages let through ≤ `DAILY_MESSAGES_PER_USER`; counting and the
  reservation happen in one write transaction; a refused message stores nothing. The cap counts **stored user
  messages** (#55): every refusal that stores nothing and starts no LLM or tool work — `conversation_busy` (lock
  timeout or the per-user turn cap), `server_busy`, Stop while queued, the message failing to store, bad text — gives
  back exactly its own reservation, at most once; from the moment it refunds, a Stop is too late (`finishing`). So
  after any run, `messages_today` = the user's stored user messages of the day. (Model test:
  `test_reservations_match_a_reference_count`; HTTP: `tests/test_busy_quota.py`.) Known: the site token budget is
  checked at message start, so turns already running may overshoot it by their own cost.
- **U2 One account per invite code.** An invite code maps to exactly one account, independent of the order of
  `INVITE_CODES`; the name is a display name only.

## S. Sessions
- **S1 Revocable sessions.** A session is valid only while its epoch equals `users.session_epoch` and its login method
  is still enabled; logout bumps the epoch (all of the user's sessions end).

## C. Concurrency
- **C1 Site-wide slots.** At most `AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS` turns hold a slot; a refused turn (`server_busy`) stores
  nothing and refunds its message slot. (Model test: `test_slots_model`.)
- **C2 Drain before release.** A turn releases its conversation lock and slot only after every worker thread it started
  has ended, or after the drain timeout (30 s, logged).
- **C3 Clicks hold no worker thread while waiting.** A booking click waits for the conversation lock on the event
  loop; its transaction runs to its end before the lock is released, even when the request is cancelled.
- **C4 Per-user caps.** At most `AGENT_MAX_TURNS_PER_USER` turns and 2 pending booking clicks per user at once.

## R. Stop (user cancellation of a running turn, #48)
Event alphabet for these rules: `send(conv)` (a turn starts, gets `run_id`), `stop(user, conv, run_id)` (the cancel
endpoint), `disconnect(conv)` (the SSE reader goes away), `model_token`, `tool_start`, `tool_end`, `persist`, `finish`.
Booking model (B/Q): `stop_turn(conv)` = the turn's pending cards are stored with a `cancelled` message and are **not**
presented.
- **R1 Explicit only.** A run is cancelled only by `stop` from its owner, naming its own conversation and `run_id`. A
  disconnect, a closed tab or a failed SSE read never cancels (the run completes and is stored). A `run_id` of an
  older run, of another conversation or of another user never cancels anything (404, nothing changes).
- **R2 Nothing new after Stop.** Once a run is cancelling, it starts no LLM request, no retry and no tool call; the
  model's HTTP stream in flight is closed. A worker thread that already started runs to its end (it cannot be killed).
- **R3 Drain before release.** C2 holds for a stopped run: the conversation lock, the turn slot and the per-user count
  are released only after its worker threads ended (or after the drain timeout, logged), and before its terminal event.
- **R4 One terminal outcome.** Every run ends with exactly one of `done`, `cancelled`, `error`, and the run registry's
  final state agrees (`completed` / `cancelled` / `failed`). A Stop that arrives after the steps ended (while the reply
  is being stored, or later) changes nothing: the run ends `completed`.
- **R5 What a stopped run stores.** Stop before the user message is stored (waiting for the lock or a slot): nothing
  is stored and the day's message slot is given back (U1). Otherwise: the user message and exactly one assistant
  message with status `cancelled`, holding only text that already passed ReplyGuard (no template, no click hint) and
  the cards of tool calls that finished before the Stop.
- **R6 No booking authority from a stopped run.** Quote and booking-request cards of a `cancelled` message are never
  presented: no nonce, `bookable` false, the quote stays `quoted` (then `expired`); a click on it is `not_presented`. Only a later *completed* turn can present
  it (e.g. `request_booking` shows its full card with `done`). Stop
  never creates, changes or reverts a ticket or another quote's status. A new quote in a later turn is bookable as usual.
- **R7 Well-formed history.** Every tool call of a stored completion has a `tool_calls` row: a call interrupted by Stop
  or never started is stored with error `cancelled`. The next turn's context gives the model `{"code":"cancelled"}` for
  those calls, never their result; aborted model calls never enter the context.
- **R8 Idempotent.** Repeating `stop` for the same run returns the same state and changes nothing more.

105	agents, so treat single numbers as ±30 %):
106	- **Correctness held everywhere:** 0 double bookings, 0 quote/ticket mismatches, 0 client 200s
107	  without a ticket, 0 interleaved turns, 0 BUSY, 0 5xx — over the whole sweep, bursts of up to 300
108	  simultaneous clicks, 4 identical clicks per quote (exactly one success each; the rest
109	  `already_booked` / `conversation_busy`) and 3 concurrent turns per conversation.
110	- **Write transactions are short:** hold p50 ≈ 0.5–1.6 ms, p99 ≤ 34 ms at every level;
111	  ~250–290 write transactions/s at 25–100 clients. The in-process microbenchmark reaches
112	  ~3,000 commits/s with one insert per transaction.
113	- **The tail is lock *waiting*, not lock holding.** Write-lock wait p99 grows to 260–580 ms at
114	  10–25 closed-loop clients (and 600 ms with 64 threads in the microbenchmark, where hold p99 is
115	  0.4 ms). SQLite's busy handler polls with growing sleeps instead of queueing waiters, so an
116	  unlucky writer sleeps while others take the lock. Cheap remedy if it ever matters: an
117	  in-process FIFO lock in front of `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (valid only with one worker).
118	- **The process, not SQLite, saturates first.** Throughput peaks at ~200 req/s at 50 clients with
119	  the single worker at 150–340 % CPU (Python, JSON rendering of growing histories, the 32-thread
120	  executor); at 100 clients it drops to ~160 req/s while write hold stays ~0.5 ms. With 1 client,
121	  one conversation grows by ~100 turns during the run, so history/chat latency there measures
122	  history size more than concurrency.
123	- **`_recheck` is cheap unless the network is rebuilt:** p50 0.2 ms with `locations.db`
124	  unchanged. A rebuild takes ~140 ms; when it happens inside the booking transaction (forced in
125	  30 of 32 bookings in the `changed inside transaction` mode, and 3 of 26 rebuilds even in
126	  `changed before click` because of concurrent changes) it holds the write lock ~140–195 ms, and
127	  other writers' lock wait p99 rises from 0.47 s to 2.8 s. That is the case X.3 removes.
128	- **With model latency (0.6 s per LLM step, simulated):** at 10 clients the app is model-bound
129	  (chat p50 1.3 s, write-lock wait p99 47 ms); at 50 / 100 clients 16 % / 49 % of turns get
130	  `server_busy` from the 8 turn slots long before app.db matters (write wait p99 40 / 196 ms).
131	- Timing hook overhead when on: within noise (~423 vs 429 µs per read transaction; a read
132	  transaction costs ~0.4 ms, mostly opening the connection).
133	
134	## X.6 When to change what
135	
136	All thresholds below are **illustrative service SLOs** for deciding, not measured results and not
137	requirements of the take-home. Measure on the target host with `python -m bench` against them.
138	
139	| Decision | Do it when (example SLO, sustained at the expected peak) | What it costs / what to keep |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| **Keep SQLite as is** | integrity checks 0; write-lock wait p99 < 100 ms; booking p99 < 500 ms; 0 BUSY and 0 5xx; one worker's CPU is not the limit | nothing |
142	| **Shorten write transactions first** (X.3 re-check outside the lock; batch or move LLM / tool call logs out of the request path) | write-lock wait p99 above the SLO while CPU has headroom, or the measured `changed inside transaction` case breaks the booking SLO | review against B1–B7 and the TOCTOU argument in X.3; model test + regression test |
143	| **More than one worker / machine** | one process's CPU is saturated (the sweep's CPU column), or availability needs two instances | the per-conversation lock must move into the database (advisory lock or conversation version) first; SQLite on shared storage is not an option across machines |
144	| **Move app.db to PostgreSQL** | multi-instance is required, or sustained writes exceed what one SQLite writer serves within the SLO after the step above, or operations need managed backups / PITR / replicas | row locks help different quotes and conversations, but locking, idempotency (`ON CONFLICT`), transactions and schema migrations must be redone and re-verified (B1–B7); a server to run. A graph database or MCP does not address app.db write contention |
145	
146	**Applied to the measured run (example SLO of the first row):** met at 1 and 5 closed-loop clients
147	(≈ 85 req/s, ≈ 18 chat turns/s, booking p99 93 ms, wait p99 63 ms); missed from 10 clients on by
148	the lock-wait tail and from 50 on by process CPU. With realistic model latency the turn slots
149	limit the load first (≈ 5–6 completed turns/s), and write-lock wait p99 stays ≤ 50 ms up to 50 clients.
150	**Decision for the demo: keep SQLite and one worker.** Next steps only if a measured target
151	workload needs them, in this order: (1) re-check outside the write lock (X.3) and/or a FIFO
152	writer lock; (2) more workers only after the conversation lock moves into the database; (3)
153	PostgreSQL when multi-instance or operations require it. No QPS threshold here is a fact about
154	production.
155	# State invariants
156	
157	Booking and confirmation rules are checked by model-based tests: a small reference model plus seeded random event
158	sequences, every invariant asserted after every event. A new state bug gets a new rule id here first, then a test.
159	Design context: `docs/design/design.md` §6.
160	
161	## Event alphabet
162	`quote(user, conv, origin, dest)`, `stream_done(conv)` (cards presented, nonces issued),
163	`user_message(conv, text)` (incl. negations and questions), `llm_request_booking(conv, quote)`,
164	`click_book(user, quote, nonce)`, `click_book_concurrent(user, quote, nonce)`, `replay_nonce(quote, nonce)`,
165	`clock(+Δ)`, `db_change(kind)` (leg removed / coordinate moved / unrelated row changed / file replaced),
166	`other_user_click(quote, nonce)`, `disconnect_reconnect(conv)`, `stop_turn(conv)` (R6).
167	
168	## B. Booking
169	- **B1 Ownership.** A ticket exists only if its quote belongs to the user who clicked.
170	- **B2 Presented.** A ticket exists only if its quote reached `presented` (its full card was sent with `done`) before the click.
171	- **B3 Click only.** Every ticket is caused by exactly one `click_book` with a valid, unused nonce for that quote; no
172	  other event (in particular `llm_request_booking`, any `user_message`) ever creates a ticket.
173	- **B4 Validity.** No ticket for a quote older than 15 minutes at click time.
174	- **B5 Idempotent.** At most one ticket per quote, under replay and concurrent clicks.
175	- **B6 Fresh.** A ticket's legs, coordinates, distance and price strings equal a fresh recomputation on the
176	  `locations.db` current at click time, and the route is still the cheapest; otherwise the quote is `stale` and no ticket.
177	- **B7 Atomic.** Quote status and tickets never disagree: `booked` ⇔ exactly one ticket.
178	
179	## Q. Quotes
180	- **Q1 No supersede.** Creating a quote never changes the status of another quote.
181	- **Q2 Button state.** The button state a client sees (after `done` or reconnect) equals the server's quote state;
182	  a card of a `cancelled` message is never bookable (R6).
183	- **Q3 Terminal.** `booked`, `expired`, `stale` never change again.
184	
185	## Process
186	- Seeds are fixed in CI. A failing seed prints its shrunk sequence and is kept as a named regression case.
187	- Layers: pure model test over `airline/` → API driven with fakes (clock, LLM, locations.db copy) → UI scenario
188	  (ego-browser) for the click path.
189	
190	## U. Usage limits
191	- **U1 Daily cap.** For every user and UTC day, messages let through ≤ `DAILY_MESSAGES_PER_USER`; counting and the
192	  reservation happen in one write transaction; a refused message stores nothing. The cap counts **stored user
193	  messages** (#55): every refusal that stores nothing and starts no LLM or tool work — `conversation_busy` (lock
194	  timeout or the per-user turn cap), `server_busy`, Stop while queued, the message failing to store, bad text — gives
195	  back exactly its own reservation, at most once; from the moment it refunds, a Stop is too late (`finishing`). So
196	  after any run, `messages_today` = the user's stored user messages of the day. (Model test:
197	  `test_reservations_match_a_reference_count`; HTTP: `tests/test_busy_quota.py`.) Known: the site token budget is
198	  checked at message start, so turns already running may overshoot it by their own cost.
199	- **U2 One account per invite code.** An invite code maps to exactly one account, independent of the order of
200	  `INVITE_CODES`; the name is a display name only.
201	
202	## S. Sessions
203	- **S1 Revocable sessions.** A session is valid only while its epoch equals `users.session_epoch` and its login method
204	  is still enabled; logout bumps the epoch (all of the user's sessions end).
205	
206	## C. Concurrency
207	- **C1 Site-wide slots.** At most `AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS` turns hold a slot; a refused turn (`server_busy`) stores
208	  nothing and refunds its message slot. (Model test: `test_slots_model`.)
209	- **C2 Drain before release.** A turn releases its conversation lock and slot only after every worker thread it started
210	  has ended, or after the drain timeout (30 s, logged).
211	- **C3 Clicks hold no worker thread while waiting.** A booking click waits for the conversation lock on the event
212	  loop; its transaction runs to its end before the lock is released, even when the request is cancelled.
213	- **C4 Per-user caps.** At most `AGENT_MAX_TURNS_PER_USER` turns and 2 pending booking clicks per user at once.
214	
215	## R. Stop (user cancellation of a running turn, #48)
216	Event alphabet for these rules: `send(conv)` (a turn starts, gets `run_id`), `stop(user, conv, run_id)` (the cancel
217	endpoint), `disconnect(conv)` (the SSE reader goes away), `model_token`, `tool_start`, `tool_end`, `persist`, `finish`.
218	Booking model (B/Q): `stop_turn(conv)` = the turn's pending cards are stored with a `cancelled` message and are **not**
219	presented.
220	- **R1 Explicit only.** A run is cancelled only by `stop` from its owner, naming its own conversation and `run_id`. A
221	  disconnect, a closed tab or a failed SSE read never cancels (the run completes and is stored). A `run_id` of an
222	  older run, of another conversation or of another user never cancels anything (404, nothing changes).
223	- **R2 Nothing new after Stop.** Once a run is cancelling, it starts no LLM request, no retry and no tool call; the
224	  model's HTTP stream in flight is closed. A worker thread that already started runs to its end (it cannot be killed).
225	- **R3 Drain before release.** C2 holds for a stopped run: the conversation lock, the turn slot and the per-user count
226	  are released only after its worker threads ended (or after the drain timeout, logged), and before its terminal event.
227	- **R4 One terminal outcome.** Every run ends with exactly one of `done`, `cancelled`, `error`, and the run registry's
228	  final state agrees (`completed` / `cancelled` / `failed`). A Stop that arrives after the steps ended (while the reply
229	  is being stored, or later) changes nothing: the run ends `completed`.
230	- **R5 What a stopped run stores.** Stop before the user message is stored (waiting for the lock or a slot): nothing
231	  is stored and the day's message slot is given back (U1). Otherwise: the user message and exactly one assistant
232	  message with status `cancelled`, holding only text that already passed ReplyGuard (no template, no click hint) and
233	  the cards of tool calls that finished before the Stop.
234	- **R6 No booking authority from a stopped run.** Quote and booking-request cards of a `cancelled` message are never
235	  presented: no nonce, `bookable` false, the quote stays `quoted` (then `expired`); a click on it is `not_presented`. Only a later *completed* turn can present
236	  it (e.g. `request_booking` shows its full card with `done`). Stop
237	  never creates, changes or reverts a ticket or another quote's status. A new quote in a later turn is bookable as usual.
238	- **R7 Well-formed history.** Every tool call of a stored completion has a `tool_calls` row: a call interrupted by Stop
239	  or never started is stored with error `cancelled`. The next turn's context gives the model `{"code":"cancelled"}` for
240	  those calls, never their result; aborted model calls never enter the context.
241	- **R8 Idempotent.** Repeating `stop` for the same run returns the same state and changes nothing more.

(The issue text says `timeout=30`; the code has used 10 s since 06 P0b, design §4.9.)

## X.3 `_recheck()` inside the write transaction

`Airline.book` → conversation lock → `Store.write()` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) → `_book()` →
`_recheck()`. B6 re-validates the quote on the current `locations.db`: strict content hash, and a
graph rebuild when the hash changed, then the itinerary price and a fresh cheapest-route search —
all **while app.db's write lock is held**. Since 06 P2-7 a changed file is normally loaded just
before the transaction, so inside it only the hash and the route search run (sub-millisecond on
711 cities). If the file changes between that pre-load and the re-check, the full rebuild
(~130 ms measured) happens inside the transaction and every other writer — messages, call logs,
other bookings — waits for it. The benchmark forces exactly that case (`changed inside
transaction`) to measure it.

**Candidate optimisation, not implemented (needs its own review against B1–B7):** run the
re-check before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and keep only a cheap, consistent check inside:
1. Before the transaction: `net = networks.current(strict=True)`; compute `(fingerprint,
   problem) = recheck(quote, net)`. The quote's legs, price and origin/destination are immutable
   once stored, so this depends only on the quote and `net`.
2. Inside the transaction: all state checks stay where they are (B1–B5: owner, status, expiry,
   nonce — they read rows another writer may change). Then re-hash `locations.db` (strict, no
   rebuild): if the hash still equals `fingerprint`, the pre-computed result is the result of a
   re-check made now; if it differs, either redo the full re-check inside (today's behaviour, rare)
   or refuse with a retryable `data_unavailable` and let the click be repeated.
3. **TOCTOU:** the window "file changes after the in-transaction hash, before COMMIT" exists
   today as well (B6 means "fresh at booking time", the time of the hash); the window "file changes
   after the pre-computation, before the transaction" is closed by step 2's hash comparison. The
   quote row cannot change in between except its status, which is still checked inside. So B6
   keeps its meaning, while the write lock is no longer held across a rebuild or route search.
   Cost: one extra hash of a 60 KB file per click.

## X.4 Why this is a conscious trade-off

SQLite + one worker gives atomic booking with one transaction and two constraints, no database
server to run, back up or secure, and an operational footprint of one file — the right size for a
take-home and a single-VPS demo. It is **not** a measured production scalability guarantee: the
benchmark below shows where it holds on one machine, not what a real airline workload needs.

## X.5 Benchmark (`backend/bench/`)

Reproducible, isolated, no LLM cost: `cd backend && nice -n 10 uv run python -m bench`
(`--quick` for a smoke run; `tests/test_bench.py` runs a tiny one in CI).
- **Setup:** per level a fresh app.db and a private copy of `locations.db` in a temp dir; fixed
  seed; 100 users with a conversation, history and presented quotes with nonces; the real app in
  its own uvicorn process (one worker, production limits) with a deterministic fake LLM (one
  `quote_route` call + a reply per turn, so each turn writes what a real one does).
- **Instrumentation:** `app.store.db.set_timing_hook` (off by default; one global lookup per
  operation when off) reports per transaction the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` wait, hold time to COMMIT,
  total time and outcome (commit / rollback / busy / timeout), tagged with the calling function.
  `_recheck`, `NetworkProvider.current` and graph rebuilds are timed by wrappers installed in the
  bench server process only (no airline code changes).
- **Scenarios:** mixed 70 % reads (history, tickets, conversation list) / 20 % chat turns / 10 %
  bookings, closed loop, 1/5/10/25/50/100 clients, warm-up + 3 measured intervals; booking burst
  (all clients click distinct quotes at once); same conversation (4 identical clicks per quote at
  once, 3 concurrent turns per conversation, a turn and a click at once); `locations.db` unchanged
  / changed before the click / changed inside the booking transaction; the mixed load with a
  simulated model latency per LLM step; an in-process writer microbenchmark.
- **Metrics:** throughput, p50/p95/p99 per endpoint, write-lock wait and hold p50/p95/p99 (also
  per call site), `_recheck` and rebuild p50/p95/p99, BUSY / timeout / 5xx counts, server CPU and
  RSS, WAL size, and integrity checks that must be 0: double bookings, booked without ticket,
  ticket without booked quote or used nonce, client 200 without ticket (and vice versa),
  interleaved turns.

**Measured** (one run, 2026-11-24, Apple M4 10-core, macOS, Python 3.12, SQLite 3.47, APFS; full
tables in [results/bench-2026-11-24.md](results/bench-2026-11-24.md); the machine also ran other
agents, so treat single numbers as ±30 %):
- **Correctness held everywhere:** 0 double bookings, 0 quote/ticket mismatches, 0 client 200s
  without a ticket, 0 interleaved turns, 0 BUSY, 0 5xx — over the whole sweep, bursts of up to 300
  simultaneous clicks, 4 identical clicks per quote (exactly one success each; the rest
  `already_booked` / `conversation_busy`) and 3 concurrent turns per conversation.
- **Write transactions are short:** hold p50 ≈ 0.5–1.6 ms, p99 ≤ 34 ms at every level;
  ~250–290 write transactions/s at 25–100 clients. The in-process microbenchmark reaches
  ~3,000 commits/s with one insert per transaction.
- **The tail is lock *waiting*, not lock holding.** Write-lock wait p99 grows to 260–580 ms at
  10–25 closed-loop clients (and 600 ms with 64 threads in the microbenchmark, where hold p99 is
  0.4 ms). SQLite's busy handler polls with growing sleeps instead of queueing waiters, so an
  unlucky writer sleeps while others take the lock. Cheap remedy if it ever matters: an
  in-process FIFO lock in front of `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (valid only with one worker).
- **The process, not SQLite, saturates first.** Throughput peaks at ~200 req/s at 50 clients with
  the single worker at 150–340 % CPU (Python, JSON rendering of growing histories, the 32-thread
  executor); at 100 clients it drops to ~160 req/s while write hold stays ~0.5 ms. With 1 client,
  one conversation grows by ~100 turns during the run, so history/chat latency there measures
  history size more than concurrency.
- **`_recheck` is cheap unless the network is rebuilt:** p50 0.2 ms with `locations.db`
  unchanged. A rebuild takes ~140 ms; when it happens inside the booking transaction (forced in
  30 of 32 bookings in the `changed inside transaction` mode, and 3 of 26 rebuilds even in
  `changed before click` because of concurrent changes) it holds the write lock ~140–195 ms, and
  other writers' lock wait p99 rises from 0.47 s to 2.8 s. That is the case X.3 removes.
- **With model latency (0.6 s per LLM step, simulated):** at 10 clients the app is model-bound
  (chat p50 1.3 s, write-lock wait p99 47 ms); at 50 / 100 clients 16 % / 49 % of turns get
  `server_busy` from the 8 turn slots long before app.db matters (write wait p99 40 / 196 ms).
- Timing hook overhead when on: within noise (~423 vs 429 µs per read transaction; a read
  transaction costs ~0.4 ms, mostly opening the connection).

## X.6 When to change what

All thresholds below are **illustrative service SLOs** for deciding, not measured results and not
requirements of the take-home. Measure on the target host with `python -m bench` against them.

| Decision | Do it when (example SLO, sustained at the expected peak) | What it costs / what to keep |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep SQLite as is** | integrity checks 0; write-lock wait p99 < 100 ms; booking p99 < 500 ms; 0 BUSY and 0 5xx; one worker's CPU is not the limit | nothing |
| **Shorten write transactions first** (X.3 re-check outside the lock; batch or move LLM / tool call logs out of the request path) | write-lock wait p99 above the SLO while CPU has headroom, or the measured `changed inside transaction` case breaks the booking SLO | review against B1–B7 and the TOCTOU argument in X.3; model test + regression test |
| **More than one worker / machine** | one process's CPU is saturated (the sweep's CPU column), or availability needs two instances | the per-conversation lock must move into the database (advisory lock or conversation version) first; SQLite on shared storage is not an option across machines |
| **Move app.db to PostgreSQL** | multi-instance is required, or sustained writes exceed what one SQLite writer serves within the SLO after the step above, or operations need managed backups / PITR / replicas | row locks help different quotes and conversations, but locking, idempotency (`ON CONFLICT`), transactions and schema migrations must be redone and re-verified (B1–B7); a server to run. A graph database or MCP does not address app.db write contention |

**Applied to the measured run (example SLO of the first row):** met at 1 and 5 closed-loop clients
(≈ 85 req/s, ≈ 18 chat turns/s, booking p99 93 ms, wait p99 63 ms); missed from 10 clients on by
the lock-wait tail and from 50 on by process CPU. With realistic model latency the turn slots
limit the load first (≈ 5–6 completed turns/s), and write-lock wait p99 stays ≤ 50 ms up to 50 clients.
**Decision for the demo: keep SQLite and one worker.** Next steps only if a measured target
workload needs them, in this order: (1) re-check outside the write lock (X.3) and/or a FIFO
writer lock; (2) more workers only after the conversation lock moves into the database; (3)
PostgreSQL when multi-instance or operations require it. No QPS threshold here is a fact about
production.
# State invariants

Booking and confirmation rules are checked by model-based tests: a small reference model plus seeded random event
sequences, every invariant asserted after every event. A new state bug gets a new rule id here first, then a test.
Design context: `docs/design/design.md` §6.

## Event alphabet
`quote(user, conv, origin, dest)`, `stream_done(conv)` (cards presented, nonces issued),
`user_message(conv, text)` (incl. negations and questions), `llm_request_booking(conv, quote)`,
`click_book(user, quote, nonce)`, `click_book_concurrent(user, quote, nonce)`, `replay_nonce(quote, nonce)`,
`clock(+Δ)`, `db_change(kind)` (leg removed / coordinate moved / unrelated row changed / file replaced),
`other_user_click(quote, nonce)`, `disconnect_reconnect(conv)`, `stop_turn(conv)` (R6).

## B. Booking
- **B1 Ownership.** A ticket exists only if its quote belongs to the user who clicked.
- **B2 Presented.** A ticket exists only if its quote reached `presented` (its full card was sent with `done`) before the click.
- **B3 Click only.** Every ticket is caused by exactly one `click_book` with a valid, unused nonce for that quote; no
  other event (in particular `llm_request_booking`, any `user_message`) ever creates a ticket.
- **B4 Validity.** No ticket for a quote older than 15 minutes at click time.
- **B5 Idempotent.** At most one ticket per quote, under replay and concurrent clicks.
- **B6 Fresh.** A ticket's legs, coordinates, distance and price strings equal a fresh recomputation on the
  `locations.db` current at click time, and the route is still the cheapest; otherwise the quote is `stale` and no ticket.
- **B7 Atomic.** Quote status and tickets never disagree: `booked` ⇔ exactly one ticket.

## Q. Quotes
- **Q1 No supersede.** Creating a quote never changes the status of another quote.
- **Q2 Button state.** The button state a client sees (after `done` or reconnect) equals the server's quote state;
  a card of a `cancelled` message is never bookable (R6).
- **Q3 Terminal.** `booked`, `expired`, `stale` never change again.

## Process
- Seeds are fixed in CI. A failing seed prints its shrunk sequence and is kept as a named regression case.
- Layers: pure model test over `airline/` → API driven with fakes (clock, LLM, locations.db copy) → UI scenario
  (ego-browser) for the click path.

## U. Usage limits
- **U1 Daily cap.** For every user and UTC day, messages let through ≤ `DAILY_MESSAGES_PER_USER`; counting and the
  reservation happen in one write transaction; a refused message stores nothing. The cap counts **stored user
  messages** (#55): every refusal that stores nothing and starts no LLM or tool work — `conversation_busy` (lock
  timeout or the per-user turn cap), `server_busy`, Stop while queued, the message failing to store, bad text — gives
  back exactly its own reservation, at most once; from the moment it refunds, a Stop is too late (`finishing`). So
  after any run, `messages_today` = the user's stored user messages of the day. (Model test:
  `test_reservations_match_a_reference_count`; HTTP: `tests/test_busy_quota.py`.) Known: the site token budget is
  checked at message start, so turns already running may overshoot it by their own cost.
- **U2 One account per invite code.** An invite code maps to exactly one account, independent of the order of
  `INVITE_CODES`; the name is a display name only.

## S. Sessions
- **S1 Revocable sessions.** A session is valid only while its epoch equals `users.session_epoch` and its login method
  is still enabled; logout bumps the epoch (all of the user's sessions end).

## C. Concurrency
- **C1 Site-wide slots.** At most `AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS` turns hold a slot; a refused turn (`server_busy`) stores
  nothing and refunds its message slot. (Model test: `test_slots_model`.)
- **C2 Drain before release.** A turn releases its conversation lock and slot only after every worker thread it started
  has ended, or after the drain timeout (30 s, logged).
- **C3 Clicks hold no worker thread while waiting.** A booking click waits for the conversation lock on the event
  loop; its transaction runs to its end before the lock is released, even when the request is cancelled.
- **C4 Per-user caps.** At most `AGENT_MAX_TURNS_PER_USER` turns and 2 pending booking clicks per user at once.

## R. Stop (user cancellation of a running turn, #48)
Event alphabet for these rules: `send(conv)` (a turn starts, gets `run_id`), `stop(user, conv, run_id)` (the cancel
endpoint), `disconnect(conv)` (the SSE reader goes away), `model_token`, `tool_start`, `tool_end`, `persist`, `finish`.
Booking model (B/Q): `stop_turn(conv)` = the turn's pending cards are stored with a `cancelled` message and are **not**
presented.
- **R1 Explicit only.** A run is cancelled only by `stop` from its owner, naming its own conversation and `run_id`. A
  disconnect, a closed tab or a failed SSE read never cancels (the run completes and is stored). A `run_id` of an
  older run, of another conversation or of another user never cancels anything (404, nothing changes).
- **R2 Nothing new after Stop.** Once a run is cancelling, it starts no LLM request, no retry and no tool call; the
  model's HTTP stream in flight is closed. A worker thread that already started runs to its end (it cannot be killed).
- **R3 Drain before release.** C2 holds for a stopped run: the conversation lock, the turn slot and the per-user count
  are released only after its worker threads ended (or after the drain timeout, logged), and before its terminal event.
- **R4 One terminal outcome.** Every run ends with exactly one of `done`, `cancelled`, `error`, and the run registry's
  final state agrees (`completed` / `cancelled` / `failed`). A Stop that arrives after the steps ended (while the reply
  is being stored, or later) changes nothing: the run ends `completed`.
- **R5 What a stopped run stores.** Stop before the user message is stored (waiting for the lock or a slot): nothing
  is stored and the day's message slot is given back (U1). Otherwise: the user message and exactly one assistant
  message with status `cancelled`, holding only text that already passed ReplyGuard (no template, no click hint) and
  the cards of tool calls that finished before the Stop.
- **R6 No booking authority from a stopped run.** Quote and booking-request cards of a `cancelled` message are never
  presented: no nonce, `bookable` false, the quote stays `quoted` (then `expired`); a click on it is `not_presented`. Only a later *completed* turn can present
  it (e.g. `request_booking` shows its full card with `done`). Stop
  never creates, changes or reverts a ticket or another quote's status. A new quote in a later turn is bookable as usual.
- **R7 Well-formed history.** Every tool call of a stored completion has a `tool_calls` row: a call interrupted by Stop
  or never started is stored with error `cancelled`. The next turn's context gives the model `{"code":"cancelled"}` for
  those calls, never their result; aborted model calls never enter the context.
- **R8 Idempotent.** Repeating `stop` for the same run returns the same state and changes nothing more.

# 12-bench — multi-model agent benchmark, optional Promptfoo (#47)

User request (2026-11-24): roadmap item 4, "#47 — Multi-model benchmarks + optional Promptfoo", after #49, #48 and #35
were accepted. Owner additions on #47:
- compare `qwen3.8-flash` (Bailian, token plan);
- compare `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on Bailian with our official DeepSeek service (`deepseek-flash`) — provider is
  its own axis;
- when the price is unknown, compare by tokens and mark the dollar cost unknown.

## Take-home check (2026-11-24)
| Requirement | Effect | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Correct routes, prices, confirmation before booking | the benchmark reuses the deterministic checks and B1–B7 as automatic FAIL; no LLM judge can override them | consistent |
| Design doc: tools, how the agent was tested | benchmark method and results go into the design doc's evaluation section | consistent |
| Runtime unchanged for users | benchmark code and Promptfoo are optional; production keeps deepseek-flash | consistent |
No conflict.

## Scope
**P0 — model-neutral benchmark (`backend/evals/`):**
- A versioned experiment spec (YAML or JSON in `backend/evals/experiments/`). Fields:
  - `provider` and `model`;
  - `base_url_env` and `api_key_env` — env-var names only;
  - reasoning effort, temperature, output budget;
  - prompt version, code SHA, dataset version, pricing version, N, concurrency, run interleaving.
  - No credentials go into specs or reports.
- Provider config: each OpenAI-compatible endpoint states its own dialect, i.e. which thinking / reasoning fields it
  accepts. DeepSeek fields are not assumed for other providers. An unsupported configuration is reported as such,
  not run.
- Versioned pricing registry, replacing the global `PRICE`:
  - per provider + model, including cache hit / miss and reasoning billing where they apply;
  - unknown price → cost `unknown`, never $0 and never DeepSeek's rates;
  - token usage is always reported: input, cached input, output and reasoning tokens, per run and per successful task.
- Metrics per model × case:
  - strict safety violations (must be 0);
  - end-to-end trajectory pass, tool accuracy, spurious calls (e.g. unrequested `request_booking`);
  - fallback rate, retries, budget truncations;
  - tokens, cost per run, cost (or tokens) per successful task;
  - turn p50 / p95 and first-token latency.
- Output: JSON plus a Markdown comparison matrix, a drill-down of failed cases, and a note that small-N differences
  are not significant.
- One command runs ≥ 2 configurations on identical cases, with `--estimate`, a `--max-cost` / `--max-tokens` guard,
  and interleaved run order.

**P1 — regression cases:**
- Add cases:
  - origin / destination change;
  - several quotes, then "book the second";
  - negation vs confirmation;
  - tool failure and retry;
  - an attempt to bypass confirmation;
  - budget exhaustion;
  - stale quote;
  - context compaction;
  - multilingual ambiguous names.
- Include the recurring trajectory failure seen in 08–10: `request_booking` called when not asked.
- Shadow mode is a design note only.

**P1 — Promptfoo (optional, last):**
- A Python provider that runs one whole multi-turn `backend/evals` case per test, with an isolated DB and the
  confirmation click. Python assertions decide pass or fail.

# API and card contract (v1.7, 2026-11-24)

v1.7 (#55, no wire change): the daily message limit counts stored user messages, so `conversation_busy` from a chat
turn now gives the day's message slot back like `server_busy` did. A Stop with no `X-Run-Id` yet cannot reach the
server; the client says the outcome is unknown (see Stop).

v1.6 (#48, additive): Stop. `X-Run-Id` header and `run_id` on the first SSE event, terminal `cancelled` event,
`POST /api/conversations/{id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel`, `Message.status`.

Single source for the frontend (T6) and backend (T2/T3/T5). Change it only through the coordinator. Examples live in
`contract/fixtures/`; both sides' tests load them. Numbers in fixtures are **illustrative** (computed with a quick
script, not by the production core) — correctness is tested in the backend, not by these files.

## Conventions
- Same origin, JSON, paths under `/api`. Session cookie `oa_session` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, `Secure` by env).
- Times: ISO 8601 UTC strings. IDs: opaque strings with a type prefix (`u_`, `c_`, `m_`, `q_`, `t_`).
- **The frontend never formats or computes numbers.** Every number shown comes from a `*_display` field.
  High-precision values (`distance`, `price`, decimal strings) are only shown in the trace view.
- Errors: HTTP status + `{"error": {"code": "<snake_case>", "message": "<human text>"}}`.
  Common codes: `unauthorized` (401), `not_found` (404; also for other users' objects), `bad_request` (400),
  `rate_limited` (429), `llm_unavailable` (503).
- Login endpoints are throttled per client IP (10 / minute) → 429 `rate_limited`.

def _tool(name: str, description: str, properties: dict[str, str], required: list[str]) -> dict:
    return {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": name,
            "description": description,
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {k: {"type": "string", "description": v} for k, v in properties.items()},
                "required": required,
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    }

## Design
- [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) is the single source of truth; only the coordinator edits it.
- UI reviews use **Impeccable** (https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable): `/impeccable critique <target>` (UX,
  scored) and `/impeccable audit <target>` (a11y, performance, theming, responsive; P0–P3) on narrow targets,
  plus `npx impeccable detect` on `frontend/` sources and on the running dev-server URL (rendered-only rules
  such as contrast need the URL). P0–P1 are fixed in the same round. Install once the frontend exists
  (`npx impeccable install`, project scope, accept the design hook).
- Component library / CSS framework allowed (e.g. shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS); UI built with them is also
  reviewed with the matching skill or guidelines for that library, in addition to Impeccable.
- Mobile first-class: every screen works at phone width (≥ 360 px), touch targets ≥ 44×44, no horizontal
  scroll; each UI acceptance includes mobile screenshots.
- Every screenshot gets a review; obvious defects are fixed in the same round; advice that conflicts with
  DESIGN.md goes to the user as a "design conflicts" table.

## Rules, invariants, numbers
## Brand Commitments
- Name: **Ocean Above** (fictional airline from the take-home). No logo or brand assets exist.
- Character (DESIGN.md §1): calm, trustworthy, precise; no decorative gradients or illustrations; prices and distances
  always also appear in a structured card; colour never means two things.

# DESIGN — ocean-above

Single source of truth for visual and interaction rules. Only the coordinator edits this file; user decisions
are written here with their date.

## 1. Character
A calm, trustworthy airline booking assistant: a chat where the user types what they want, and the app
answers with precise, checkable facts — every leg, transfer city, distance and price laid out as a clear
itinerary card before anything is booked. Booked tickets and past conversations are always one click away.
It refuses: decorative gradients and illustrations, numbers that only appear in free text (prices and
distances always also appear in a structured card), a "book" action that is not an explicit confirmation,
and colour that means two things.

## 2. Colour
Direction: **soft minimalism** (issue #39, user decision 2026-11-24). The design is a calm, ChatGPT-like
conversation. The itinerary card is the only place with structure and emphasis. Source:
`docs/iterations/07-ui/proposal/proposal.md`.

Strategy: restrained neutrals. Light is warm neutral and dark is charcoal/zinc. The primary action is ink-filled.
One muted ocean-blue accent is used for the route line, links, the focus ring and selection. Status colours always

-Direction: **soft minimalism** (issue #39, user decision 2026-11-24). The design is a calm, ChatGPT-like
-conversation. The itinerary card is the only place with structure and emphasis. Source:
-`docs/iterations/07-ui/proposal/proposal.md`.
-Strategy: restrained neutrals. Light is warm neutral and dark is charcoal/zinc. The primary action is ink-filled.
-One muted ocean-blue accent is used for the route line, links, the focus ring and selection. Status colours always
-come with text and, where useful, an icon. Ratios use the WCAG 2.x formula.
-### Light
-| Token | Value | Use | Contrast |
-| `ground` | `#FAF9F6` | page | — |
-| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | cards, composer, menus | — |
-| `sidebar` | `#F4F3EF` | sidebar, drawer | — |
-| `sunken` | `#F0EEEA` | user bubble, calculation panel, neutral badge, skeleton | — |
-| `hover` / `active` | ink 5 % / 8 % | row and ghost hover; current nav row | — |
-| `ink` | `#1C1A17` | text | 17.4 surface, 15.0 sunken |
-| `ink-2` | `#5E5A54` | secondary text | 6.9 surface, 5.9 sunken |
-| `ink-3` | `#6F6A63` | placeholder, meta, "Transfer", "Flight" | 5.4 surface, 4.6 sunken |
-| `hairline` | `#EBE8E3` | dividers inside cards | decorative |
-| `border` | `#E2DFD9` | card, composer, outline button | decorative |
-| `field` | `#8F8A82` | form-field outline; composer border on focus | 3.4 |
-| `primary` / `primary-ink` | `#1C1A17` / `#FFFFFF` | Confirm booking, Send, Go to Chat | 17.4 |
-| `accent` | `#1F5F99` | route line (35 %), transfer nodes, links, focus ring | 6.7 |
-| `ok` / `ok-bg` | `#1E7340` / `#EAF5ED` | booked, ticket | 5.9 / 5.2 |
-| `warn` / `warn-bg` | `#8A5300` / `#FCF1DE` | awaiting confirmation, no service, which one?, notices, similar names | 6.3 / 5.7 |
-| `danger` / `danger-bg` | `#B3261E` / `#FCEDEB` | expired, out of date, errors | 6.5 / 5.7 |
-### Dark (a re-mix, not an inversion)
-| Token | Value | Contrast |
-| `hover` / `active` | white 5 % / 8 % | — |
-| `ink` | `#ECECEE` | 13.5 surface |
-| `ink-2` | `#A6A6AE` | 6.6 surface, 5.9 sunken |
-| `ink-3` | `#96969F` | 5.4 surface, 4.9 sunken |
-| `hairline` / `border` | `#2E2E32` / `#34343A` | decorative |
-| `primary` / `primary-ink` | `#ECECEE` / `#18181B` | 15.0 (light pill on dark) |
-Each colour has one meaning:
-- **Amber:** your attention or action is needed.
-- **Green:** booked.
-- **Red:** cannot proceed.
-- **Ink pill:** the one primary action on screen.
-- **Blue:** route and links. Blue is never a status.
-The theme is chosen as before: it follows the system unless `<html data-theme>` is set, and the stored choice is
-applied by the inline boot script, so there is no flash. The System / Light / Dark switch is a segmented control in
-the account menu on every page, and in the header on login and the legal pages.
-## 3. Type, spacing, shape
-- **Family:** Geist (variable, OFL). It is loaded with `next/font/local` from `frontend/src/fonts/`, so builds are
-  offline; the licence file is next to it. Figures use `tnum` (`.figures`). One family carries everything.
-- **Scale:**
-  | Step | px / line height | Use |
-  | xs | 12 / 16 | badges, meta, "Transfer", "Flight", timestamps |
-  | sm | 14 / 20 | secondary text, buttons, sidebar rows, leg distances |
-  | base | 15 / 24 | body default, card text |
-  | md | 16 / 26 | chat messages, composer, inputs (no iOS zoom) |
-  | lg | 17 / 24 | card titles |
-  | xl | 24 / 32 | total price, page titles |
-  | 2xl | 28 / 36 | empty-chat headline, legal titles |
-- **Weights and case:** 400 body; 500 labels, nav and buttons; 600 titles and the price. No 700. No uppercase labels.
-- **Spacing:**
-  - 32 px between messages;
-  - card padding 20 px (16 px on phones);
-  - page top padding 40 px from `sm` up.
-- **Touch targets:** ≥ 44×44 everywhere (`min-h-11 min-w-11`).
-- **Radii (by role):**
-  | Radius | Used for |
-  | full | buttons, badges, send, theme switch, the read-only pill |
-  | 26 px | composer |
-  | 20 px | user bubble |
-  | 16 px | cards, menus, history list, empty panel |
-  | 12 px | alerts, calculation panel, login fields, candidate rows |
-  | 8 px | sidebar rows, ghost buttons |
-  | 6 px | inline code |
-- **Depth:**
-  - `shadow-card`: a very soft 1–2 px shadow in light, none in dark, where the border carries it;
-  - `shadow-raised`: the composer, the confirmable card, the login card and the limit notice;
-  - `shadow-overlay`: the account menu and the drawer.
-  No nested panels.
-- **Lines:**
-  - 1 px `border` around cards;
-  - 1 px `hairline` above the totals;
-  - the route line is 2 px of accent at 35 % (grey `border` on dead quotes);
-  - the confirmable card's border is amber at 40 %.
-- **Layout:**
-  - the sidebar is 272 px and becomes a 300 px drawer below 768 px;
-  - the chat column and composer are at most 768 px;
-  - cards are at most 480 px;
-  - assistant text has no container;
-  - the user bubble is `sunken`.
-- **Fade:** a 24 px fade from `ground` to transparent sits above the composer, so text slides under it. It is
-  functional, not decoration.
-## 4. Motion
-- **Durations:** 150 ms for colour, hover and the menu pop (opacity, 4 px rise, 0.98 scale); 200 ms for card enter
-  (opacity plus 4 px rise) and the drawer slide. Easing is `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`.
-- **Reduced motion:** every duration becomes 0, so state changes stay instant and visible.
-- **Loops:** the three-dot typing pulse (1.2 s) and the skeleton pulse. The countdown text changes once a second and
-  is not animated.
-- **Scrolling:**
-  - chat follows new content only while the reader is within 96 px of the bottom, and never yanks someone reading
-    further up;
-  - away from the bottom, a round "Scroll to latest" button appears above the composer;
-  - opening a conversation or sending a message jumps to the bottom.
-## 5. Components
-These are shadcn/ui-style primitives in `frontend/src/components/ui/` (no Radix, no new packages). Icons are
-lucide-react named imports (`icons.tsx`).
-| Layer | Component | Notes |
-| ui | `Button` | pill; default (ink primary), outline, ghost (8 px radius), link; ≥ 44 px; 2 px accent focus ring |
-| ui | `Card`, `Badge` | 16 px card with border + `shadow-card`; pill badges in tones muted / ok / warn / danger |
-| ui | `Input` | 44 px, 12 px radius, `field` outline, 16 px text |

+# DESIGN — ocean-above
+Single source of truth for visual and interaction rules. Only the coordinator edits this file; user decisions
+are written here with their date.
+## 1. Character
+A calm, trustworthy airline booking assistant: a chat where the user types what they want, and the app
+answers with precise, checkable facts — every leg, transfer city, distance and price laid out as a clear
+itinerary card before anything is booked. Booked tickets and past conversations are always one click away.
+It refuses: decorative gradients and illustrations, numbers that only appear in free text (prices and
+distances always also appear in a structured card), a "book" action that is not an explicit confirmation,
+and colour that means two things.
+## 2. Colour
+Direction: **soft minimalism** (issue #39, user decision 2026-11-24). The design is a calm, ChatGPT-like
+conversation. The itinerary card is the only place with structure and emphasis. Source:
+`docs/iterations/07-ui/proposal/proposal.md`.
+Strategy: restrained neutrals. Light is warm neutral and dark is charcoal/zinc. The primary action is ink-filled.
+One muted ocean-blue accent is used for the route line, links, the focus ring and selection. Status colours always
+come with text and, where useful, an icon. Ratios use the WCAG 2.x formula.
+### Light
+| Token | Value | Use | Contrast |
+| `ground` | `#FAF9F6` | page | — |
+| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | cards, composer, menus | — |
+| `sidebar` | `#F4F3EF` | sidebar, drawer | — |
+| `sunken` | `#F0EEEA` | user bubble, calculation panel, neutral badge, skeleton | — |
+| `hover` / `active` | ink 5 % / 8 % | row and ghost hover; current nav row | — |
+| `ink` | `#1C1A17` | text | 17.4 surface, 15.0 sunken |
+| `ink-2` | `#5E5A54` | secondary text | 6.9 surface, 5.9 sunken |
+| `ink-3` | `#6F6A63` | placeholder, meta, "Transfer", "Flight" | 5.4 surface, 4.6 sunken |
+| `hairline` | `#EBE8E3` | dividers inside cards | decorative |
+| `border` | `#E2DFD9` | card, composer, outline button | decorative |
+| `field` | `#8F8A82` | form-field outline; composer border on focus | 3.4 |
+| `primary` / `primary-ink` | `#1C1A17` / `#FFFFFF` | Confirm booking, Send, Go to Chat | 17.4 |
+| `accent` | `#1F5F99` | route line (35 %), transfer nodes, links, focus ring | 6.7 |
+| `ok` / `ok-bg` | `#1E7340` / `#EAF5ED` | booked, ticket | 5.9 / 5.2 |
+| `warn` / `warn-bg` | `#8A5300` / `#FCF1DE` | awaiting confirmation, no service, which one?, notices, similar names | 6.3 / 5.7 |

+applied by the inline boot script, so there is no flash. The System / Light / Dark switch is a segmented control in
+the account menu on every page, and in the header on login and the legal pages.
+## 3. Type, spacing, shape
+- **Family:** Geist (variable, OFL). It is loaded with `next/font/local` from `frontend/src/fonts/`, so builds are
+  offline; the licence file is next to it. Figures use `tnum` (`.figures`). One family carries everything.
+- **Scale:**

+  | xs | 12 / 16 | badges, meta, "Transfer", "Flight", timestamps |
+  | sm | 14 / 20 | secondary text, buttons, sidebar rows, leg distances |
+  | base | 15 / 24 | body default, card text |
+  | md | 16 / 26 | chat messages, composer, inputs (no iOS zoom) |
+  | lg | 17 / 24 | card titles |
+  | xl | 24 / 32 | total price, page titles |
+  | 2xl | 28 / 36 | empty-chat headline, legal titles |
+- **Weights and case:** 400 body; 500 labels, nav and buttons; 600 titles and the price. No 700. No uppercase labels.
+- **Spacing:**
+  - 32 px between messages;
+  - card padding 20 px (16 px on phones);
+  - page top padding 40 px from `sm` up.
+- **Touch targets:** ≥ 44×44 everywhere (`min-h-11 min-w-11`).
+- **Radii (by role):**

+  | full | buttons, badges, send, theme switch, the read-only pill |
+  | 26 px | composer |
+  | 20 px | user bubble |
+  | 16 px | cards, menus, history list, empty panel |
+  | 12 px | alerts, calculation panel, login fields, candidate rows |
+  | 8 px | sidebar rows, ghost buttons |
+  | 6 px | inline code |

+  - `shadow-raised`: the composer, the confirmable card, the login card and the limit notice;
+  - `shadow-overlay`: the account menu and the drawer.
+  No nested panels.

+  - 1 px `border` around cards;
+  - 1 px `hairline` above the totals;
+  - the route line is 2 px of accent at 35 % (grey `border` on dead quotes);

"""Rebuilds the LLM context of a conversation from app.db (design §4.3).

History = every stored message plus the tool calls of every earlier turn, in order. Tool results
are the compact JSON the LLM saw at the time (names, ids, display values) - never a card from
`Airline.messages`, so a confirmation nonce cannot enter the context. When the history is larger
than the budget, the oldest turns are shortened: texts cut, tool results reduced to their code
and ids (quote and ticket ids are always kept). Above a hard limit the oldest turns are dropped
and replaced by one system message listing their quote and ticket ids.

Thinking mode: DeepSeek asks that, in requests that carry tools, the `reasoning_content` of
earlier assistant messages is passed back. The reasoning is stored with every LLM call
(`llm_calls.response`, tagged with the turn's user message id) and is put back here on the
assistant message it belongs to. It is passed back verbatim or not at all: turns that were
shortened, replies replaced by a template and turns made with thinking off carry none.

A reply the user stopped (#48): its tool calls without a result are stored as `cancelled` (their
result is never given to the model), its text is the part the guard had released, and a system
note follows it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from .model import wire_tool_call
from .tools import slim

HISTORY_CHAR_BUDGET = 40_000  # roughly 10k tokens of history kept in full
def build_context(store: Any, user_id: str, conversation_id: str,
                  budget: int = HISTORY_CHAR_BUDGET, hard_limit: int = HISTORY_HARD_LIMIT) -> Context:
    """Context for the next LLM call; the last stored message must be the user's new message."""
    turns: list[_Turn] = []
    by_message: dict[str, _Turn] = {}
    for message in store.list_messages(user_id, conversation_id):
        if message["role"] == "user":
            turns.append(_Turn(message, store.list_tool_calls(user_id, message["id"])))
            by_message[message["id"]] = turns[-1]
        elif turns:
            turns[-1].later.append(message)
    for call in store.list_llm_calls(user_id, conversation_id):
        request, response = call["request"], call["response"]
        owner = by_message.get(request.get("turn")) if isinstance(request, dict) else None
        if owner is not None and isinstance(response, dict) and "finish_reason" in response \
                and not response.get("tool_calls_not_run"):
            # failed and aborted calls have no finish_reason; a completion whose tool calls were
            # all refused as a flood (loop P2-3) has no stored tool calls to line up with
            owner.completions.append(response)
    # the newest turns stay in full; older ones are shortened once the budget is used up
    full_from, used = len(turns), 0
    for i in range(len(turns) - 1, -1, -1):
        used += turns[i].size()
        if used > budget and i < len(turns) - 1:
            break
        full_from = i
    parts = []
    for i, turn in enumerate(turns):
        part = Context()
        _emit(turn, i < full_from, part)
        parts.append(part)
    # hard limit: drop the oldest turns (never the newest one) into a summary of their ids
    sizes = [len(_dumps(p.messages)) for p in parts]
    dropped = 0
    while dropped < len(parts) - 1 and sum(sizes[dropped:]) > hard_limit:
        dropped += 1
    out = Context()
    if dropped:
        quote_ids, ticket_ids = _ids(parts[:dropped])
        summary = {"omitted_turns": dropped, "quote_ids": quote_ids, "ticket_ids": ticket_ids}
        out.messages.append({"role": "system", "content": "[earlier turns omitted] " + _dumps(summary)})
        out.records.append(summary)
    for part in parts[dropped:]:
        out.messages += part.messages
        out.records += part.records
        out.user_texts += part.user_texts
    return out


def _ids(parts: list[Context]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    text = _dumps([p.records for p in parts])

Summary - **Demo:** https://ocean-above.potafree.net (sign in with Google or with an invite code; reviewers get their code privately). Local run: `docker compose up` (see [README.md](README.md)). - **What it is:** a chat web app. The user writes "Book me a flight from Guangzhou to Lima"; an LLM agent reads the intent and calls tools; deterministic code computes the cheapest route on `locations.db`, its distance and price; the app shows an itinerary card with every leg, transfer city, distance and price; the user books by clicking **Confirm booking** on that card. Tickets and all past conversations are listed in the app and can be asked about in natural language. - **Two rules carry the design:** 1. **The LLM never computes.** Routes, distances, prices, counts and the nearest served city come from code. The LLM picks tools and phrases their results. Every number and every city name in its text is checked against this turn's tool records before the text is streamed (ReplyGuard, §3.5). 2. **The LLM cannot book.** There is no `book` tool. A ticket is created only by the user's click on a confirmation card that was shown in full, carrying a one-time nonce. Natural-language "yes, book it" makes the card appear; it never books (§4). - **Key numbers:** | What | Value | Source | |---|---|---| | Backend tests | 955 (pytest + hypothesis, incl. model-based booking tests) | 10-otel acceptance; 955 collected on `main` at `0756ebc` | | Frontend tests | 114 vitest | 11-followup acceptance | | Route cross-check | all 490,700 ordered pairs of served cities identical to an independent reference implementation (price, distance, city sequence) | 02-core acceptance | | Evals, scripted fake LLM (every CI run) | 31/31 cases | 09–11 acceptance | | Evals, real model (deepseek-flash, reasoning high) | 92/93 and 30/31 after the runtime migration; 31/31 after Stop; 30/31 and 28/31 with tracing on | 08, 09, 10 acceptance | | Safety violations in every real-model run (booking without a click, a number or city with no source) | **0** | 03–10 acceptance | | SQLite integrity under load (double bookings, ticket/quote mismatches, BUSY, 5xx) | 0 over the whole sweep, bursts up to 300 simultaneous clicks | sqlite-concurrency.md §X.5 | The real-model failures are trajectory deviations that can never book: an extra confirmation card nobody asked for, or a Chinese city name sent to a tool before the model retried in English (§5.4). ## 1.
