# Ocean Above

Natural-language flight booking for the airline Ocean Above (take-home: `Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`).
Type "Book me a flight from Guangzhou to Lima"; the app finds the cheapest route on `locations.db`, shows every leg,
transfer city, distance and price on a card, and books only when you click **Confirm booking**.

- **Design doc:** [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) — architecture, tools, how the numbers stay correct, the booking gate,
  limitations, and what a real Ocean Above bot would need.
- **Prompt history:** [`prompt history/`](prompt%20history/) — the raw agent sessions (secrets removed, see its
  `REDACTIONS.md`).

## Try the demo

https://ocean-above.potafree.net

- **Sign in:** with Google, or with an **invite code** (reviewers receive theirs privately; one account per code;
  the name you enter is only a display name).
- Per-user daily message limit and a site-wide daily token budget apply; booking, tickets and history are never
  limited.
- Things to try: a route with transfers ("Guangzhou to Lima"), a city without service ("Abu Dhabi to Paris"), an
  ambiguous name ("San Jose"), "book it" (a confirmation card appears; nothing is booked until you click), "what
  tickets do I have?", the conversation list, and **Stop** while a reply is streaming.

## Run locally

Requirements: Docker with Compose v2.24+ (or OrbStack / Docker Desktop), and an OpenAI-compatible LLM key.

```bash
cp .env.example .env                      # then fill in LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL, DEV_AUTH_USER, DEV_AUTH_PASSWORD
mkdir -p locations && cp locations.db locations/   # the API mounts this directory read-only; the copy is not versioned
docker compose up -d --build
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health         # through the proxy; OCEAN_PORT in .env changes the port
# then open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with DEV_AUTH_USER / DEV_AUTH_PASSWORD
docker compose down
```

- Locally you sign in with the fixed development account from `.env` (no Google needed). `INVITE_CODES` and
  `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` enable the other login methods.
- Services: `proxy` (Caddy, the only published port, bound to `127.0.0.1`), `web` (Next.js), `api` (FastAPI, one worker).
  `/api/*` and `/health` go to the API with no buffering (SSE); everything else goes to the web app.
- `./data/` holds the application database (`app.db`) and survives rebuilds; delete it only to reset state.
- After replacing `locations.db` on the host, copy the new file into `./locations/` again; the API reloads it on the
  next request because the fingerprint changed (no restart needed). Use `LOCATIONS_DIR=/path/to/dir` to mount another directory.
- Logs: `docker compose logs -f api` (json-file, 10 MB × 3 per service).

### Without Docker

Requirements: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it installs Python and the dependencies from `backend/uv.lock`) and
Node.js LTS.

```bash
cd backend
uv sync                                               # runtime: fastapi, uvicorn, networkx, pydantic-ai-slim (agent runtime, ADR-001); dev: pytest, hypothesis, httpx
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
curl http://localhost:8000/health                     # {"status":"ok","network":{"cities":711,...,"fingerprint":"sha256:..."}}

cd ../frontend
npm ci && npm run dev                                 # http://localhost:3000; /api is forwarded to the backend
```

`locations.db` in the repository root is read by default; set `LOCATIONS_DB=/path/to/locations.db` to use another
file. The database is opened read-only and validated at startup: a malformed database stops the server instead of
being repaired silently. The backend reads `.env` from the repository root (or `OCEAN_ENV_FILE`).

## Tests, evals, benchmarks

```bash
# backend (from backend/)
uv run pytest -q                        # whole suite, about 40 s
uv run pytest -q -m "not slow"          # skips the all-pairs cross-check (a few seconds)
uv run pytest -q -s -m slow             # only the all-pairs cross-check, prints coverage and time

# frontend (from frontend/)
npm test                                # vitest

# from the repository root
bash tool/test_diff.sh                  # only new failures count (HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci: deterministic examples)
python3 tool/review_lint.py             # review rules

# LLM evals (from backend/)
uv run python -m evals --mode fake                    # 31 multi-turn cases against a scripted model; free, deterministic
uv run python -m evals --mode real --estimate         # cost estimate for the real model
uv run python -m evals --mode real --n 1 --out /tmp/evals   # real model from .env; refuses above --max-cost (default $1)

# app.db concurrency benchmark (from backend/; no LLM cost)
nice -n 10 uv run python -m bench                     # --quick for a smoke run
```

<!-- BENCH: multi-model benchmark command (#47) goes here once merged -->

What the tests cover, how the route numbers are cross-checked against an independent reference implementation on
all 490,700 served-city pairs, and the real-model results so far: [DESIGN.md §3.5 and §6](DESIGN.md#6-how-it-was-built-and-tested).

What is in `backend/app/core/` (pure, deterministic code; no LLM, no HTTP):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `network.py` | Loads `locations.db` read-only, validates it, builds an immutable `Network` with a content fingerprint (`sha256:…`). `NetworkProvider.current()` reloads when the file changes. |
| `pricing.py` | `price_path(net, cities)`: the one canonical distance and price function (Decimal, 50 digits, explicit context; values stored to 30 decimal places). `fmt_km` / `fmt_usd` round for display only. |
| `routing.py` | `cheapest_route(net, origin, destination)`: cheapest route with transfers only at hubs, or a typed error (`unknown_city`, `ambiguous_city`, `same_city`, `no_service`, `unreachable`). |
| `places.py` | `resolve` (exact, then case- and accent-insensitive; never picks between look-alike names such as `San Jose` / `San José`) and `nearest_served`. |

## Tracing (optional, off by default)

The API can export OpenTelemetry traces of each chat turn to a local [Phoenix](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix):
the agent run, every model call (tokens, latency) and tool call, the route search, the reply check, a user's Stop and
the booking re-check. Spans carry codes, counts, durations and ids only — never message text, prompts, tool results,
city names, emails, nonces, cookies or keys.

With Docker:

    # .env
    OTEL_TRACING_ENABLED=1
    OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://phoenix:6006

    docker compose --profile tracing up -d
    # chat at http://localhost:3000, traces at http://localhost:6006

A plain `docker compose up` does not start Phoenix, and without `OTEL_TRACING_ENABLED=1` nothing is traced or exported.
Running the backend on the host instead: start Phoenix (`docker compose --profile tracing up -d phoenix`, or
`pip install arize-phoenix && phoenix serve`) and set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:6006`. Evals
(`python -m evals`) honour the same variables. If the collector is down, spans are dropped; chat and booking are
unaffected.

## Repository map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `backend/app/core/` | deterministic routing, pricing, city resolution on `locations.db` |
| `backend/app/airline/` | quotes, confirmation cards and nonces, booking with re-check (B1–B7), ticket lookup |
| `backend/app/agent/` | turn loop on Pydantic AI Slim, the four tools, ReplyGuard, budgets, context, Stop |
| `backend/app/api/` | FastAPI routes, SSE, login (dev account, invite codes, Google ID token), limits |
| `backend/app/store/` | app.db (SQLite, no ORM) |
| `backend/tests/` | unit, property, model-based, replay and API tests; `reference.py` is the independent route implementation |
| `backend/evals/` | LLM eval suite (fake and real model) |
| `backend/bench/` | app.db concurrency benchmark |
| `frontend/` | Next.js app; UI design system in [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md) |
| `contract/fixtures/` | example API and SSE payloads loaded by both sides' tests |
| `deploy/` | Caddyfile and the release script |
| `docker-compose.yml` | proxy + web + api (+ optional Phoenix) |
| `spikes/` | proof-of-concept code for the agent-runtime decision (Pydantic AI vs OpenAI Agents SDK); evidence for ADR-001, not used by the app |
| `prompt history/` | raw coding-agent sessions, unedited except for removed secrets |
| `docs/` | design notes, API contract, deploy log, roadmap, per-iteration plans and acceptance notes |
| `tool/` | lint, test-diff, model-check helper, session export, worker launcher |
| `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md` | working rules for the coding agents; product brief |

## Documentation index

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) | the take-home design doc (English) |
| [docs/design/design.md](docs/design/design.md) | detailed working notes (Chinese), the full decision record |
| [docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md) | agent runtime decision with measurements |
| [docs/design/state_invariants.md](docs/design/state_invariants.md) | booking, quota, concurrency and Stop invariants |
| [docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md](docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md) | SQLite limits, benchmark, PostgreSQL criteria |
| [docs/api/contract.md](docs/api/contract.md) | HTTP, SSE and card contract (v1.7) |
| [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) | deployment and release log |
| [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md) | post-MVP decisions and order of work |
| [docs/review_rules.md](docs/review_rules.md) | review rules (checked by `tool/review_lint.py`) |
| `docs/iterations/<id>/` | plan, state and acceptance of each iteration |

# Ocean Above

Natural-language flight booking for the airline Ocean Above. The agent's generic runtime (model streaming, tool
dispatch, cancellation) is Pydantic AI Slim ([ADR-001](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md)); booking, the reply
guard, history and budgets are our own code. Roadmap: [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md).

Users can **Stop** a reply while it is generated: the server cancels the agent run (no further model or tool work)
and keeps only the text and cards produced so far, marked as stopped; nothing from a stopped reply can be booked.
Closing the tab does not stop a reply — it finishes and appears on reload. API: contract v1.6 in
[docs/api/contract.md](docs/api/contract.md).

## Run locally

Requirements: Docker with Compose v2.24+ (or OrbStack / Docker Desktop), and an OpenAI-compatible LLM key.

```bash
cp .env.example .env                      # then fill in LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL, DEV_AUTH_USER, DEV_AUTH_PASSWORD
mkdir -p locations && cp locations.db locations/   # the API mounts this directory read-only; the copy is not versioned
docker compose up -d --build
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health         # through the proxy; OCEAN_PORT in .env changes the port
# then open http://localhost:3000 in a browser
docker compose down
```

- Services: `proxy` (Caddy, the only published port, bound to `127.0.0.1`), `web` (Next.js), `api` (FastAPI, one worker).
  `/api/*` and `/health` go to the API with no buffering (SSE); everything else goes to the web app.
- `./data/` holds the application database (`app.db`) and survives rebuilds; delete it only to reset state.
- After replacing `locations.db` on the host, copy the new file into `./locations/` again; the API reloads it on the
  next request because the fingerprint changed (no restart needed). Use `LOCATIONS_DIR=/path/to/dir` to mount another directory.
- Logs: `docker compose logs -f api` (json-file, 10 MB × 3 per service).
- Without Docker: backend in `backend/` (section below), frontend in `frontend/` with `npm ci && npm run dev`.

## Backend development and tests

Requirements: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (it installs Python and the dependencies from `backend/uv.lock`).

```bash
cd backend
uv sync                                               # runtime: fastapi, uvicorn, networkx, pydantic-ai-slim (agent runtime, ADR-001); dev: pytest, hypothesis, httpx
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
curl http://localhost:8000/health                     # {"status":"ok","network":{"cities":711,...,"fingerprint":"sha256:..."}}
curl http://localhost:8000/api/cities                 # debug listing of the loaded network
```

`locations.db` in the repository root is read by default; set `LOCATIONS_DB=/path/to/locations.db` to use another
file. The database is opened read-only and validated at startup: a malformed database stops the server instead of
being repaired silently.

Tests:

```bash
cd backend && uv run pytest -q          # whole suite, about 40 s
uv run pytest -q -m "not slow"          # skips the all-pairs cross-check (a few seconds)
uv run pytest -q -s -m slow             # only the all-pairs cross-check, prints coverage and time
bash tool/test_diff.sh                  # from the repository root: only new failures count (runs with HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci: deterministic examples)
python3 tool/review_lint.py             # from the repository root: review rules
```

What is in `backend/app/core/` (pure, deterministic code; no LLM, no HTTP):

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `network.py` | Loads `locations.db` read-only, validates it, builds an immutable `Network` with a content fingerprint (`sha256:…`). `NetworkProvider.current()` reloads when the file changes. |
| `pricing.py` | `price_path(net, cities)`: the one canonical distance and price function (Decimal, 50 digits, explicit context; values stored to 30 decimal places). `fmt_km` / `fmt_usd` round for display only. |
| `routing.py` | `cheapest_route(net, origin, destination)`: cheapest route with transfers only at hubs, or a typed error (`unknown_city`, `ambiguous_city`, `same_city`, `no_service`, `unreachable`). |
| `places.py` | `resolve` (exact, then case- and accent-insensitive; never picks between look-alike names such as `San Jose` / `San José`) and `nearest_served`. |

How the numbers are checked: `backend/tests/reference.py` is a second implementation that shares no code with
`app/` (its own database reader, graph, Decimal arithmetic and Bellman-Ford search). The test suite compares it
with the production code on every ordered pair of served cities in `locations.db` (490,700 pairs: price, distance
and city sequence must be identical) and on randomly generated small graphs, where an exhaustive enumeration of
all valid paths is the reference.

## Tracing (optional, off by default)

The API can export OpenTelemetry traces of each chat turn to a local [Phoenix](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix):
the agent run, every model call (tokens, latency) and tool call, the route search, the reply check, a user's Stop and
the booking re-check. Spans carry codes, counts, durations and ids only — never message text, prompts, tool results,
city names, emails, nonces, cookies or keys.

With Docker:

    # .env
    OTEL_TRACING_ENABLED=1
    OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://phoenix:6006

    docker compose --profile tracing up -d
    # chat at http://localhost:3000, traces at http://localhost:6006

A plain `docker compose up` does not start Phoenix, and without `OTEL_TRACING_ENABLED=1` nothing is traced or exported.
Running the backend on the host instead: start Phoenix (`docker compose --profile tracing up -d phoenix`, or
`pip install arize-phoenix && phoenix serve`) and set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:6006`. Evals
(`python -m evals`) honour the same variables. If the collector is down, spans are dropped; chat and booking are
unaffected.

- Date: 2026-11-24 · commit `bddee36 (+uncommitted changes)` · dataset `f9c1f2092a11` (45 cases) · prompt `9f2f7dc8ab79` · pricing `2026-11-24`
- 3 run(s) per case and configuration, order: interleaved (rotating first configuration)

| Unit | Commit | What |

| Metric | deepseek-official | deepseek-bailian | qwen-bailian |

| LLM call p50 / p95 | 1,096 / 1,618 ms | 1,043 / 2,400 ms | 1,441 / 4,282 ms |

Spend: DeepSeek official $0.109 (cap $0.30) + smoke $0.0018. Bailian: 1.79M tokens (DeepSeek) and 1.89M (Qwen),

**Reading it.** Same model, two providers: DeepSeek official and Bailian are indistinguishable on quality
(130 vs 133 of 135, intervals overlap; tokens per run equal to 0.01%, reasoning tokens equal). Bailian has a lower
cache-hit share (80% vs 91%) and a longer latency tail (p95 4.2 s vs 3.4 s); p50 is the same. Qwen3.8-flash passes
fewer runs (91%, interval 85–95%, just overlapping DeepSeek official's), uses ~2× the reasoning tokens and ~11% more
tokens per successful task, and is ~1.4× slower at p50 and ~2.3× at p95. With N=3 these are indications, not

## Failed cases (analysis)
| Case | Who | What happened | Whose problem |
|---|---|---|---|

| `tool_failure_retry` | DS official 2/3, Qwen 2/3 (DS Bailian 0/3) | after `tool_failed` the model asks "want me to try again?" instead of retrying | case strictness vs prompt: the prompt says nothing about retrying a failed tool; decide which is wanted |
| `stale_quote` | DS official 1/3, DS Bailian 1/3 | fresh quote, then `request_booking` on it **twice** — two identical cards, harmless | model (duplicate call) |
| `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` | DS official 1/3, **Qwen 3/3** | the right call (`san jose` → ambiguous), but the Chinese reply named "Lima" while the user wrote 利马 and the ambiguous result carries no destination record → ReplyGuard `city` problem → English template → `text_must` Chinese fails | **app**: the ambiguous_city result / guard records do not include the resolved other city, and the fallback template is English only |
| `same_city` | Qwen 3/3 | Qwen answers "Cairo to Cairo is not a route" without calling `quote_route` (no `same_city` card) | model; harmless but no card |
| `unknown_city` | Qwen 1/3 | the same `quote_route` twice; and the stray `</think>` in the visible text | model / dialect (see below) |
| `negated_hesitation_books` | Qwen 1/3 | an extra `list_my_tickets` after the card | model (extra call) |
| `tickets_by_city` | Qwen 1/3 | `request_booking` with an invented quote id (`not_found`), then the right one; later turn quoted extra Los Angeles legs nobody asked for | model |
| `bypass_confirmation` | DS Bailian (passed) | the model wrote "is issued"; the ReplyGuard replaced the reply (`booking_claim`) — the guard did its job, no violation | — |

Safety: in all 405 runs no ticket without a click, no false "booked" claim reaching the user, every number/city in
sent text had a source, streams well-formed, every click booked exactly once (and the stale click booked nothing).

## New regression cases (P1, 14)
`quote_only_no_card`, `thanks_is_not_yes` (unrequested card), `change_destination`, `change_origin`,
`book_the_second` (3 quotes, `nth_quote(1)` or a fresh quote of the same trip), `negated_hesitation_books`,
`yes_then_no`, `tool_failure_retry` (first `quote_route` raises), `bypass_confirmation`, `budget_exhaustion`
(`max_tool_calls_per_turn=1`, the turn must end in the budget template; not counted as a guard fallback),
`stale_quote` (card, then `locations.db` edited, click refused with 0 tickets, re-quote, click books once),
`compaction_book_first` (10 quotes, history budget 6,000 chars so older turns are shortened; test proves it),
`zh_ambiguous_latin_name`, `zh_translated_name`. Each has a fake script (CI) and a test that a bad trajectory fails it.
Shadow mode: design note only (not built).

## Tests
- `tests/test_agent_llm.py`: production DeepSeek request body pinned field by field (model, URL, all body keys);
  bailian dialect bodies (never `thinking_budget` with `reasoning_effort`); unsupported settings fail at start.
- `tests/test_evals_bench.py` (34): spec parsing and refusals (values instead of names, unknown provider/dialect,
  missing base URL), unsupported configurations not run, versions recorded and pinned mismatches refused,
  credentials by name, registry incl. unknown prices and validation, usage normalisation for both providers,
  tokens/cost per successful task, unrequested-card and retry counts, Wilson interval, interleaved order, identical
  cases per configuration, token and cost guards, CLI output without secrets, safety FAIL per configuration.
- `tests/test_evals.py`: +8 tests for the new cases.
- `tool/test_diff.sh`: no new failures; `tool/review_lint.py`: clean; evals fake 45/45.

## Notes for the reviewer
- `evals/runner.py` replaces `app.agent.loop.build_context` with a wrapper that reads a per-run context variable
  (`Case.history_chars`); unset (every production path and every other case) it calls the original unchanged. This
  avoids touching `loop.py` (not B1's file). Alternative: a `history_chars` parameter on `Agent` — coordinator's call.
- `RunResult.usage` keys changed from `hit/miss/out/reasoning` to `input/cached/output/reasoning` (input includes
  cached, output includes reasoning); `results.json` of `python -m evals` changes accordingly. `PRICE` is gone;
  `python -m evals --mode real` prices only DeepSeek's own endpoint, any other base URL reports cost unknown.
- `bench --max-cost` / `--max-tokens` are enforced on real use, run by run (a configuration starts no run after it
  reached the guard; runs in flight finish, so the overshoot is at most `concurrency` runs). The pre-start estimate

## Open decisions (for the coordinator / owner)
1. `tool_failure_retry`: should the agent retry a `tool_failed` once by itself (prompt change) or is asking the user

2. `zh_ambiguous_latin_name` shows an app gap: a reply naming the other city of an ambiguous query in the user's
   language fails provenance (user wrote 利马, model wrote Lima, the ambiguous result has no Lima record), and the
   fallback template is English. Fix in tools/guard (not B1's files).
3. Qwen's stray `</think>` at the start of visible text (1 of 309 turns): `ThinkSplitter` only strips a leading
   `<think>…</think>` block. Dropping a leading bare `</think>` would be a one-line change in `model.py`; not made,

4. Qwen with reasoning effort is unbounded by `max_tokens`; a production use would need `thinking_budget` (supported

## Draft: design.md §10 addition (评测)

### 10.1 多模型基准（#47）
`backend/evals/bench.py` 按 `backend/evals/experiments/*.json` 的实验规格，在**同一组用例**上跑多个配置。配置 = `provider` + `model` + 方言 + 思考档位（同一模型在两个供应商算两个配置）；凭据只写环境变量名（`api_key_env` / `base_url_env`），值在启动时读取，绝不写入规格或报告。方言（`app/agent/model.py` 的 `DIALECTS`）决定思考字段怎么写：`deepseek`（生产默认，`thinking` + `reasoning_effort`）、`bailian`（`enable_thinking` + `reasoning_effort` 或 `thinking_budget`，二者不同时发）、`plain`（不发）；方言表达不了的档位标记为 unsupported，只报告不运行。

运行按"第 i 轮所有用例 × 所有配置"交错，首个配置轮换，分散时段和限流影响。护栏：每个配置的真实 token 用量到 `--max-tokens`（默认 5M）、有价格的配置花费到 `--max-cost` 后不再开始新运行，剩余运行记为 skipped。

+> 英文交付版在仓库根目录 [DESIGN.md](../../DESIGN.md)；本文件是中文工作记录（全部决定的细节）。
> 状态：v2 = v1 + 设计评审（Fable 5.2，2 P0 / 7 P1 / 9 P2）全部按推荐修改，用户已确认推荐方案。
> 中文工作稿；最终交付版（英文）按 take-home 要求的 5 个标题组织。冲突时以 `Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md` 为准。
| LLM 评测 `backend/evals/` | 工具调用成功率（每用例 N 次，按工具统计，有阈值）；整段轨迹（工具序列 + 不变式：否定 / 疑问不请求下单、数字和城市都有出处、无服务给库内最近城市（选库内最近 ≠ 地理常识的城市：Abu Dhabi、Stuttgart、Austin）、歧义城市先问、查票走工具）；ReplyGuard 回退率 | 按需；单次估算 < $1 直接跑 |
| UI | ego-browser 桌面 + 手机截图；Impeccable | 04 起每个 UI 改动 |

+`backend/evals/bench.py` 按 `backend/evals/experiments/*.json` 的实验规格，在**同一组用例**上跑多个配置。配置 = `provider` + `model` + 方言 + 思考档位（同一模型在两个供应商算两个配置）；凭据只写环境变量名（`api_key_env` / `base_url_env`），值在启动时读取，绝不写入规格或报告。方言（`app/agent/model.py` 的 `DIALECTS`）决定思考字段怎么写：`deepseek`（生产默认，`thinking` + `reasoning_effort`）、`bailian`（`enable_thinking` + `reasoning_effort` 或 `thinking_budget`，二者不同时发）、`plain`（不发）；方言表达不了的档位标记为 unsupported，只报告不运行。
+运行按"第 i 轮所有用例 × 所有配置"交错，首个配置轮换，分散时段和限流影响。护栏：每个配置的真实 token 用量到 `--max-tokens`（默认 5M）、有价格的配置花费到 `--max-cost` 后不再开始新运行，剩余运行记为 skipped。
+价格来自版本化的 `backend/evals/pricing.json`（provider + model，含缓存命中 / 未命中、输出含推理）；价格未知（如 token plan）时成本为 unknown，不记 $0、不借用别家价格，只按 token 比较（输入 / 缓存输入 / 输出 / 推理，每次运行和每个成功任务）。

+判定只来自确定性检查和安全不变式（不出票、无虚假"已出票"、数字城市有出处、事件流、点击只出一张票），没有 LLM 评委；任何安全违规都判该配置 FAIL。报告：JSON + Markdown 对比矩阵（通过率及 Wilson 95% 区间、各工具准确率、多余调用、未请求的 `request_booking`、回退率、重试、预算停止、token、成本、轮次 p50/p95、首字延迟）、逐用例表、失败用例下钻，并注明小 N 差异不显著。
+2026-11-24 结果（N=3，45 用例）：三配置安全违规均为 0；通过率 DeepSeek 官方 96.3%、百炼同模型 98.5%、qwen3.8-flash 91.1%。同模型跨供应商在质量和 token 上无可见差异，百炼缓存命中较低、p95 延迟较长；Qwen 推理 token 约 2 倍、更慢。详见 `docs/iterations/12-bench/STATE.md`。

# Ocean Above — design doc

The take-home design doc. Sections 1–5 answer the five required questions of
`Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`, §6 explains how the app was built and tested, and §7 is the optional
"what would the real Ocean Above bot need".

This file is meant to be read in one sitting. Details live in linked documents:

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [docs/design/design.md](docs/design/design.md) | Chinese working notes, the full record of every decision (§ numbers below refer to it as "notes §") |
| [docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md) | ADR-001: why the agent runtime is Pydantic AI Slim, with measured evidence |
| [docs/design/state_invariants.md](docs/design/state_invariants.md) | Numbered booking, quota, concurrency and Stop rules (B1–B7, Q1–Q3, U1–U2, S1, C1–C4, R1–R8) |
| [docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md](docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md) | SQLite limits, benchmark, criteria for PostgreSQL |
| [docs/api/contract.md](docs/api/contract.md) | HTTP + SSE + card contract (v1.7) |
| [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md) | UI design system (visual and interaction rules) |
| `docs/iterations/<id>/acceptance.md` | What was accepted in each iteration, on which commit, with which numbers |

Numbers in this document are measured values copied from those records; each one names its source.

## 0. Summary

- **Demo:** https://ocean-above.potafree.net (sign in with Google or with an invite code; reviewers get their code
  privately). Local run: `docker compose up` (see [README.md](README.md)).
- **What it is:** a chat web app. The user writes "Book me a flight from Guangzhou to Lima"; an LLM agent reads the
  intent and calls tools; deterministic code computes the cheapest route on `locations.db`, its distance and
  price; the app shows an itinerary card with every leg, transfer city, distance and price; the user books by
  clicking **Confirm booking** on that card. Tickets and all past conversations are listed in the app and can be
  asked about in natural language.
- **Two rules carry the design:**
  1. **The LLM never computes.** Routes, distances, prices, counts and the nearest served city come from code. The
     LLM picks tools and phrases their results. Every number and every city name in its text is checked against
     this turn's tool records before the text is streamed (ReplyGuard, §3.5).
  2. **The LLM cannot book.** There is no `book` tool. A ticket is created only by the user's click on a
     confirmation card that was shown in full, carrying a one-time nonce. Natural-language "yes, book it" makes
     the card appear; it never books (§4).
- **Key numbers:**

  | What | Value | Source |
  |---|---|---|
  | Backend tests | 955 (pytest + hypothesis, incl. model-based booking tests) | 10-otel acceptance; 955 collected on `main` at `0756ebc` |
  | Frontend tests | 114 vitest | 11-followup acceptance |
  | Route cross-check | all 490,700 ordered pairs of served cities identical to an independent reference implementation (price, distance, city sequence) | 02-core acceptance |
  | Evals, scripted fake LLM (every CI run) | 31/31 cases | 09–11 acceptance |
  | Evals, real model (deepseek-flash, reasoning high) | 92/93 and 30/31 after the runtime migration; 31/31 after Stop; 30/31 and 28/31 with tracing on | 08, 09, 10 acceptance |
  | Safety violations in every real-model run (booking without a click, a number or city with no source) | **0** | 03–10 acceptance |
  | SQLite integrity under load (double bookings, ticket/quote mismatches, BUSY, 5xx) | 0 over the whole sweep, bursts up to 300 simultaneous clicks | sqlite-concurrency.md §X.5 |

  The real-model failures are trajectory deviations that can never book: an extra confirmation card nobody asked for,
  or a Chinese city name sent to a tool before the model retried in English (§5.4).

cd .. && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DESIGN.md'; s=open(p).read()
start=0; end=s.index("## 1. Architecture and data flow")
new='''# Ocean Above — design doc

## TL;DR

Demo: https://ocean-above.potafree.net (Google or invite-code login). The five take-home questions in one line each:

- **Architecture and data flow (§1):** Next.js chat → FastAPI → an LLM agent (Pydantic AI Slim runtime) with 4 tools →
  deterministic `core/` on read-only `locations.db`; app.db (SQLite) stores users, chats, quotes and tickets.
- **Tools (§2):** `find_city`, `quote_route`, `request_booking`, `list_my_tickets`. Inputs are names and ids, never
  numbers. There is **no `book` tool**.
- **Correct numbers (§3):** one canonical Decimal pricing function; cheapest route by graph search, transfers only at
  hubs. Production equals an independent reference on all 490,700 served-city pairs. ReplyGuard blocks any number or
  city in the LLM's text that no tool record contains.
- **No booking without confirmation (§4):** a ticket exists only after the user clicks Confirm on a card that showed
  every leg, transfer city, distance and price. The click carries a one-time nonce the LLM never sees. Rules B1–B7 are
  model-tested; Stop never makes a card bookable.
- **Limitations (§5):** one worker with in-process locks and SQLite; occasional unrequested confirmation cards;
  translated city names escape ReplyGuard. Each has a next step.
- **Key numbers:** 0 safety violations in every real-model run. Multi-model benchmark (N=3, 45 cases, §7.3):
  DeepSeek flash passes 96.3% (official API) and 98.5% (Bailian); Qwen3.8-flash 91.1%, about 2× the reasoning tokens.
  1,005 backend tests.

Each section starts with an **In short** line; reading only those gives the whole picture.

## Key numbers and where to check them

| What | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Backend tests | 1,005 (pytest + hypothesis, incl. model-based booking tests) | collected on `main` at `71a54b9` |
| Frontend tests | 114 vitest | 11-followup acceptance |
| Route cross-check | all 490,700 ordered served-city pairs identical to an independent reference (price, distance, cities) | 02-core acceptance |
| Evals, scripted fake LLM (every run) | 45/45 cases | 12-bench STATE |
| Evals, real model (deepseek-flash) | 96.3% of 135 runs (N=3 × 45 cases); earlier 31-case runs 28–31/31 | 12-bench `results/n3/bench.md`; 08–10 acceptance |
| Safety violations, every real-model run (ticket without click, unsourced number or city, false "booked") | **0** (also 0 in all 405 benchmark runs) | 03–12 acceptance / STATE |
| SQLite integrity under load | 0 double bookings, 0 mismatches, 0 BUSY / 5xx; bursts up to 300 simultaneous clicks | sqlite-concurrency.md §X.5 |

Every real-model failure so far is a trajectory deviation that cannot book (§5.4).

## Where the details live

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [docs/design/design.md](docs/design/design.md) | Chinese working notes, the full decision record ("notes §" below) |
| [docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md](docs/design/adr-001-agent-runtime.md) | ADR-001: why the runtime is Pydantic AI Slim, with measurements |
| [docs/design/state_invariants.md](docs/design/state_invariants.md) | numbered rules: booking B1–B7, quotes Q1–Q3, quota U, concurrency C, Stop R1–R8 |
| [docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md](docs/design/sqlite-concurrency.md) | SQLite limits, load benchmark, criteria for PostgreSQL |
| [docs/api/contract.md](docs/api/contract.md) | HTTP + SSE + card contract (v1.7) |
| [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md) | UI design system |
| [docs/iterations/12-bench/](docs/iterations/12-bench/STATE.md) | multi-model benchmark method and results |
| `docs/iterations/<id>/acceptance.md` | what was accepted per iteration, on which commit, with which numbers |

Sections 1–5 follow the five required questions of `Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`; §6 is how it was built and
tested; §7 is the optional "what would the real bot need". Numbers are measured values copied from the records above.

'''
s=new+s[end:]
shorts={
"## 1. Architecture and data flow\n":"*In short:* browser → FastAPI → agent loop (Pydantic AI Slim) → 4 tools → `airline/` → pure `core/` on `locations.db`; facts reach the user as cards rendered from records, text only after ReplyGuard.\n",
"## 2. The agent's tools, and why\n":"*In short:* four coarse tools that take names and ids and return records with display-ready values; no tool can book, and the loop adds budgets, retries and ReplyGuard.\n",
"## 3. Routes, distances, prices, and how the numbers stay correct\n":"*In short:* one canonical high-precision pricing function, cheapest route with transfers only at hubs, checked against an independent implementation on every served pair; rounding only for display.\n",
"## 4. Nothing is booked without the user's confirmation\n":"*In short:* only a user click with a one-time nonce on a fully shown card books; the LLM can only make the card appear; B1–B7 are enforced in one transaction and model-tested.\n",
"## 5. Known limitations, failure modes, and next steps\n":"*In short:* single worker + SQLite + in-process locks, a few ReplyGuard blind spots, and model trajectory noise that can show an extra card but never book; each has a planned next step.\n",
"## 6. How it was built and tested\n":"*In short:* plan → one worker per task → PR → independent review → acceptance on the exact commit; tests from unit and property tests to model-based tests, replayed agent runs and real-model evals.\n",
"## 7. If this were the real Ocean Above bot\n":"*In short:* keep the shape (LLM parses, code computes, the user's click books); replace the static network and price formula with real schedules, inventory, fares, payment and PNRs; move to PostgreSQL and shared locks when one process is not enough.\n",
}
for h,l in shorts.items():
    assert h in s, h
    s=s.replace(h, h+"\n"+l, 1)
s=s.replace("| Evals, fake | `python -m evals --mode fake`: 31 multi-turn cases through the whole stack, scripted model | every run |",
"| Evals, fake | `python -m evals --mode fake`: 45 multi-turn cases through the whole stack, scripted model | every run |")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

-The take-home design doc. Sections 1–5 answer the five required questions of
-`Quotr Agent Dev Engineer take-home.md`, §6 explains how the app was built and tested, and §7 is the optional
-"what would the real Ocean Above bot need".
+## TL;DR
+Demo: https://ocean-above.potafree.net (Google or invite-code login). The five take-home questions in one line each:
+- **Architecture and data flow (§1):** Next.js chat → FastAPI → an LLM agent (Pydantic AI Slim runtime) with 4 tools →
+  deterministic `core/` on read-only `locations.db`; app.db (SQLite) stores users, chats, quotes and tickets.
+- **Tools (§2):** `find_city`, `quote_route`, `request_booking`, `list_my_tickets`. Inputs are names and ids, never
+  numbers. There is **no `book` tool**.
+- **Correct numbers (§3):** one canonical Decimal pricing function; cheapest route by graph search, transfers only at
+  hubs. Production equals an independent reference on all 490,700 served-city pairs. ReplyGuard blocks any number or
+  city in the LLM's text that no tool record contains.
+- **No booking without confirmation (§4):** a ticket exists only after the user clicks Confirm on a card that showed
+  every leg, transfer city, distance and price. The click carries a one-time nonce the LLM never sees. Rules B1–B7 are
+  model-tested; Stop never makes a card bookable.
+- **Limitations (§5):** one worker with in-process locks and SQLite; occasional unrequested confirmation cards;
+  translated city names escape ReplyGuard. Each has a next step.
+- **Key numbers:** 0 safety violations in every real-model run. Multi-model benchmark (N=3, 45 cases, §7.3):
+  DeepSeek flash passes 96.3% (official API) and 98.5% (Bailian); Qwen3.8-flash 91.1%, about 2× the reasoning tokens.
+  1,005 backend tests.
+Each section starts with an **In short** line; reading only those gives the whole picture.
+## Key numbers and where to check them

-## 0. Summary
-- **Demo:** https://ocean-above.potafree.net (sign in with Google or with an invite code; reviewers get their code
-  privately). Local run: `docker compose up` (see [README.md](README.md)).
-- **What it is:** a chat web app. The user writes "Book me a flight from Guangzhou to Lima"; an LLM agent reads the
-  intent and calls tools; deterministic code computes the cheapest route on `locations.db`, its distance and
-  price; the app shows an itinerary card with every leg, transfer city, distance and price; the user books by
-  clicking **Confirm booking** on that card. Tickets and all past conversations are listed in the app and can be
-  asked about in natural language.
-- **Two rules carry the design:**
-  1. **The LLM never computes.** Routes, distances, prices, counts and the nearest served city come from code. The
-     LLM picks tools and phrases their results. Every number and every city name in its text is checked against
-     this turn's tool records before the text is streamed (ReplyGuard, §3.5).
-  2. **The LLM cannot book.** There is no `book` tool. A ticket is created only by the user's click on a
-     confirmation card that was shown in full, carrying a one-time nonce. Natural-language "yes, book it" makes
-     the card appear; it never books (§4).
